samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
samples.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Travis Timmerman argues the series dramatizes Singer's equal consideration of interests: Zira frees Taylor once he writes 'My name is Taylor' because like interests must count equally regardless of species, while Dr. Zaius's erasing the writing, lobotomizing Landon, and destroying the cave artifacts is pure speciesism in Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' sense. He rejects the crude 'humans are smarter' argument (it would strip severely cognitively disabled humans of standing) and Nussbaum's species-normal version (it would permit caging Zira and Cornelius since normal apes are mute), then deploys Plato's Euthyphro dilemma against Locke-style God-given rights: a deity bellowing that human interests outrank ape interests is arbitrary unless grounded in independent reasons. Since farming severely cognitively disabled humans is obviously wrong and species membership is morally irrelevant, it is equally wrong to factory-farm and experiment on animals - so, like Caesar in Battle for the Planet of the Apes, become vegetarian.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Mirror, Mirror
samples.relation: Sailors convicts Dorothy of being the stereotypical female of Baum's and Fleming's versions, disowning responsibility for killing both witches and living to please others, then contrasts her with Elphaba of Wicked as a feminist hero who leaves home, protects Animals, and mixes 'hot' male and 'cold' female anger into a single fury. She reads Elphaba's indeterminate gender through Marilyn Frye's point that easily identifiable groups are the easiest to oppress, through de Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but becomes a woman' and Mill's line that the 'nature of women' is an eminently artificial thing. Singer's liberation logic, together with the Wollstonecraft-Taylor 'Vindication of the Rights of Brutes' episode and the ecofeminist link between the oppression of women and animals, is applied to Elphaba's Animal-rights activism and her position as 'neither man nor beast,' before the Witch's mirror recognition of Dorothy forces the author to soften her verdict.

samples.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
samples.title: Futurama and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter uses 'The Problem with Popplers' to map the real-world ethics of eating meat: Free Waterfall Jr.'s 'You shouldn't eat things that feel pain' restates Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's equal consideration of suffering; Fishy Joe's profits-first stance echoes agro-ecological defenses of meat eating; and Leela's 'eating an intelligent animal is different' voices the common intuition Singer condemns as speciesism. The food-chain justification collapses when the Omicronians claim the apex and demand 198 billion humans in return, and Bender's 'fight to the death and I'll cook the loser' flips the diner's perspective, while Waterfall's orangutan-for-Leela trade sets up Singer's future-directed preferences distinction from Practical Ethics as a possible rescue. The chapter ends on the episode's real target: gluttonous consumption ('stuff the ship!') and the arbitrary sentimentality governing what we will and won't eat.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: Detmer argues moral vegetarianism follows from principles nearly everyone accepts — cruelty, the infliction of unnecessary or disproportionate suffering, is wrong — and that Atkins, which escalates meat eating without being necessary for weight loss, fails both his necessity and proportion tests. Rebutting human superiority, he deploys Rachels's point that no single feature like language is relevant to every difference in treatment and Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', holds factory-farm castration without anesthetic up against the civet-cat musk trade his students already condemn, and answers Narveson's appeal to intuition and the appeal to tradition. Even granting Atkins maximal health benefits, the margin over a well-planned vegetarian diet (Denmark's WWI blockade, the Framingham data) cannot justify the animal suffering, world-hunger, and environmental costs — most of that case drawn from Singer's Animal Liberation.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Uses 'Fun with Veal' (the boys' bedroom standoff over baby calves, the FDA renaming veal 'tortured baby cows', Stan's meat strike punished by 'vaginitus'), 'Whale Whores' (the Japanese hating dolphins until Stan's doctored Enola Gay photo swaps in a cow and chicken), and 'Pee' (researchers peeing on rhesus monkeys) to pose the line-drawing problem: why do we protect cute animals and slaughter yummy ones? Neither intelligence (pigs versus dogs), utility, age, nor cuteness survives scrutiny as a morally relevant criterion — if it did, Nurse Gollum or Timmy would lose standing. Singer's speciesism analogy and the utilitarian inclusion of all who can suffer are then applied: Cartman, who draws his moral circle around himself, is the honest ethical egoist, while Kyle and Butters' selective vegetarianism and the adults' meat-eating inconsistency are exactly what Singer's view condemns.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Seth Walker asks whether Nick Van Owen - the Earth First! documentarian who monkeywrenches InGen's camp and frees the caged dinosaurs in The Lost World - is a bastard or morally justified. He runs the consequentialist cost-benefit (the escaped T. rex slaughters a cargo ship crew and trashes San Diego; the sabotage costs the team their radio and rescue) against the ecodefense argument built on Arne Naess's deep ecology and biocentric equality, on which Isla Sorna is our 'home' and rescuing the injured baby T. rex Roland Tembo crippled is Self-defense. Singer's principle of equal consideration of suffering - a difference in ability never justifies a difference in consideration - bridges the gap for those who reject biocentrism, and Walker answers the consistency objection (must Nick accept InGen sabotaging him back?) before crediting Nick's defense of his larger home.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents - rational by Aristotle's standard of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgments about evildoers tasting better) and free despite their blood-craving, since craving is a strong preference, not the compulsion of the heroin addict or the castaway drinking seawater. Since animal blood is a viable alternative (Louis's rats, Angel and Spike's butcher's blood), the justifications for drinking human blood - taste, reaching full potential, spiritual peace - all fail against the principle that a world with less unnecessary suffering is better. Then the consistency argument turns on us: factory-farmed meat inflicts unnecessary suffering for the sake of taste while vegetarianism is fully viable, so condemning vampires while eating chicken is inconsistent - we as human beings are vampiric.

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
samples.title: Captain America’s mighty S.H.I.E.L.D. . . . Well, Sort Of
samples.relation: Bogaerts asks why every proactive superhero comes to grief: Nick Fury's unauthorized Secret War in Latveria, Tony Stark's exile of the Hulk and registration crusade, and the Illuminati's blunder all backfire (World War Hulk, the Skrull invasion), and Aquinas's doctrine of double effect—elaborated by Foot and Anscombe—cannot absolve them, since the foreseen harms were massive and disproportionate to the intended goods. Comics theory supplies the deeper cause: Reynolds's status quo defense and Jewett and Lawrence's American monomyth (via Campbell's hero's journey) make the superhero genre intrinsically reactive, guarding a paradise rather than remaking it, so heroes who 'move up into governance'—Thor as Lord of Earth, the Squadron Supreme's utopia—slide into supervillainy. Foot's act/omission distinction and the priority of negative over positive duties explain the trap, and why even Steve Rogers, as the new top cop, retreats to being Captain America again.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 14. Guns Don’t Kill Colors—Colors Kill Colors
samples.relation: Robert Arp argues from Hobbes's right of nature—self-preservation as the first law found out by reason—that individuals, and by extension oppressed peoples, have a right to the means of lethal defense, so arming the lowColors of the Society is justified. He weighs pacifist counterpoints (Augustine on self-defense as inordinate self-love, the Buddhist first precept, Camus's refusal to kill) and answers with Aquinas's principle of double effect: Darrow destroying the flagship to save Luna, intending the good while foreseeing the deaths, is justified, as is killing in defense of innocent children the Institute rapes and eats. The Society then illustrates why disarmament enables tyranny—Hideyoshi's Sword Hunt, Stalin's weapons bans, the Golds' razor monopoly—so that when lowColors finally receive weapons in Morning Star they become the means by which the police state falls: guns equalize the weak against aggressors and the people against the state.

samples.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
samples.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
samples.relation: Robichaud argues Peter actually wronged two of his worst enemies before they became them. Kant's requirement to treat persons as ends, tempered by reflective equilibrium, condemns his years-long deception of best friend Harry about being Spider-Man and about Norman's death — a silence that later explodes Harry into the second Green Goblin — and having unknowingly made the sentient alien symbiote dependent on him during Secret Wars, Peter owed it more caution than blasting it off as dirty laundry. Still, two wrongs don't make a right: Harry may 'Goblinize' only in self-defense, not revenge, and by the doctrine of double effect Spider-Man may ring the bell tower to separate Venom from Eddie Brock even foreseeing the symbiote's destruction and Eddie's breakdown; finally, his special obligations oblige him to seek his friends' reform, not merely their capture.

samples.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
samples.title: Justified and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter assembles real contested self-defense cases beside Raylan's shooting of Tommy Bucks - the OK Corral and Wyatt Earp's far-from-clean vendetta ride, Curtis Reeves killing a texting moviegoer over thrown popcorn, George Zimmerman and Trayvon Martin, Ossian Sweet's mobbed house, Bernie Goetz's subway shooting, Gary Plauche executing his son's abuser on camera, and the Texas father who beat his daughter's rapist to death. Its philosophical machinery is Aquinas's principle of double effect from the Summa Theologica (self-defense may have two effects, saving one's life and slaying the aggressor, only the first intended), set against St. Augustine's condemnation of private self-defense as inordinate self-love. Florida's stand-your-ground law - where the dead man cannot tell his side - supplies the legal gray zone the show's title exploits.

samples.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Puts Aquinas's Murder Principle—the private, intentional killing of an innocent is always murder—to the Men of Mayhem, arguing the Sons lack the public authority Aquinas requires to kill even the guilty. The show itself erodes the state/private line Aquinas needs: corrupt agents Kohn and Stahl, and the CIA's Romeo Parada running the Galindo Cartel, make the badge look like no moral credential at all. The Doctrine of Double Effect sorts the rest: Jax shooting first in self-defense, Tara's morphine for the dying Unser, and Juice's hypothetical land-mine sacrifice are merely foreseen deaths, while Jax syringing Clay or Juice's intentional hanging would be murder. The chapter concludes that even if Aquinas condemns the Sons, his questions about authority, innocence, and intention are exactly the ones the show forces on viewers.

samples.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Held examines the Tuatha'an Way of the Leaf as universal pacifism grounded not in religion, utility, or rights but in the metaphysical care of the self, echoing Gandhi's idea that violence taints the soul of the doer (shown by Adan exiling Lewin for rescuing raped girls and by Aram's tragic fall). He argues the Tinkers' pacifism, while idyllic, is untenable in a broken world: through Augustine's two cities, Aquinas's natural self-preservation and doctrine of double effect, and just war theory's jus ad bellum and jus in bello, he contends intentions matter and that no hero of WoT could be a pacifist, concluding the Tinkers free-ride parasitically on those who fight the Shadow and that their peace is not real peace but self-serving order-less quiet.

samples.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
samples.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
samples.relation: Montoya tests Simon's choice to sacrifice his sanity by wearing the crown to save child Marceline against three ethical theories. Aquinas's doctrine of double effect clears him because the intended good (saving her life) outweighs the merely foreseen side effect (her tears, his possible future evils); Kant's categorical imperative rules out universalizing 'let children die to save myself,' since a world of universal using destroys the rule itself; and a fountain case where Finn must choose between world-saving plans and a drowning candy child separates act from rule utilitarianism, with rule utilitarianism preserving the duty to rescue. All three converge on the verdict that Simon, not Finn, is Ooo's greatest hero.

samples.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
samples.title: The Finder of Lost Children
samples.relation: Timothy Dean Roth reads Kill Bill as a modern Divine Comedy: Tarantino punishes by contrapasso like Dante—O-Ren dies by Japanese steel, Budd by snake, Elle by blindness, Bill by a broken heart—and both treat vengeance as a form of truth-telling and an act of love. Hattori Hanzo's warning that revenge 'is a forest' echoes Aristotle on how hard it is to set the limits of anger, while the stories-within-stories of orphaned Nikki and O-Ren enact the cycle of violence vengeance perpetuates. Against this, Aquinas's doctrine of double effect shows every one of the Bride's killings is defensive self-preservation, and the film ends where Jules's arc ends: in mercy, mutual forgiveness and a whispered 'thank you' of grace.

samples.book: 025 - The Beatles and Philosophy - Nothing You Can Think that Can't Be Thunk
samples.title: CHAPTER 4 “A REVELATION TO BEHOLD”
samples.relation: Argues that the Beatles' devotion to rock and roll was a literal religious phenomenon rather than loose metaphor: Lennon's first hearing of Elvis is analyzed as a William James-style conversion, the Radio Luxembourg broadcasts were treated 'like scripture,' Hamburg was a 'baptism by fire,' and Epstein's new suits at the Cavern were announced as 'a revelation.' Drawing on James's Varieties of Religious Experience and Pragmatism, the chapter reads Beatlemania's screaming crowds as collective ecstatic ritual and the 'toppermost of the poppermost' chant as the will-to-believe making its own truth, in the way James says truth 'happens' to an idea. Aristotle's four causes supply the metaphysical frame — the 'magic' of Liverpool and the sacred quality fans reported are formal-final causation against the material-efficient causation of disenchanted modernity — while the band's double irony ('tarrying with the negative,' after Hegel) let them hold skepticism inside belief, as in Lennon's 'flaming pie' origin parody and the 'more popular than Jesus' episode.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Extra Time
samples.relation: Kent argues soccer is Aristotle's favorite sport because everything in both is organized around the goal: the four causes explain shinguards (plastic, curved shape, Mitre's workers, protection) and the game itself, with the final cause—scoring—defining a thing's identity and goodness, so two differently made balls are both soccerballs if kicked toward a net. Soccer best fulfills sport's three purposes (physical and moral discipline, theatrical imitation with catharsis, recreation): its ninety minutes of uninterrupted continuity force hundreds of renewed acts of self-mastery in Aristotle's sense of courage and the right amount, its single referee with limited powers embodies Aristotle's preferred limited monarchy, and Argentina's sportsmanlike throw-in returning the ball after Cameroon kicks it out for an injured player exemplifies equity—making a rightful exception to the letter of the law. Own goals, where a defender's error harms his own side, supply the hamartia of Aristotelian tragedy, giving fans a healthy catharsis of pity and fear.

samples.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
samples.title: One Thing We Know Is That Life Is Strange
samples.relation: Donovan and Richardson read Jason Aaron and Chris Bachalo's 2015 comic run as portraying Strange as a natural philosopher-scientist: he researches the Book of Vishanti to trap Zelma Stanton's mind maggots, combines inductive and deductive reasoning, and must eventually write new laws of magic when the old books fail. Aristotle's four causes and teleology are applied concretely — Strange spares the Een'Gawori slugs because their end or purpose is merely to consume magic (acorns cannot be conquerors), letting him deduce something else destroyed their homeworld — with Aquinas credited for mediating Aristotle to Christendom. Lord Imperator and the Empirikul embody a fanatical, inquisitional 'science' (draining magic from Fandazar Foo and the Sanctum, unleashing the Thing in the Cellar), contrasted with the genuinely entwined history of science, philosophy, and magic from Copernicus, Bacon, Galileo, and Kepler through Descartes and Newton to quantum 'spooky action' — Clarke's law that advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 30 - “The Golden Man”
samples.relation: Jeremy Pierce reads 'The Golden Man' through the Aristotle-Lucretius dispute over purposes in nature: Cris Johnson, the precognitive golden mutant, first terrifies the DCA as Homo superior, 'a deeve who would be to us what we are to the great apes', until George Baines finds 'virtually no frontal lobe... It's nothing but an animal' choosing by reflex rather than reflection. Aristotle's teleology - normal development suiting what is objectively good for a human being - makes sense of calling one-armed growth, autism's deficits, or Cris's missing inner life deficiencies, while Lucretius's anti-teleology, largely adopted by the autism community, permits talk only of the typical and atypical. The chapter argues the characters' horror at humanity's replacement by reflex-driven breeders is unintelligible unless something is genuinely missing that is natural and healthy for human offspring.

samples.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
samples.title: 3 The Virtues that Made the Man, and the Man Who Became the Legend The Adventures in Philosophy of Young India
samples.relation: Robert Mentyka reads The Adventures of Young Indiana Jones through Aristotle: Kazantzákis's causality lesson in 'Travels with Father' introduces the four causes, which the chapter applies to the TV series itself, and the final cause grounds ethics — eudaimonia is the ultimate end of all action, as young Indy learns when the Mata Hari affair in 'Demons of Deception' shows that pleasure cannot deliver fulfillment. Virtue is a mean between extremes (courage between cowardice and recklessness), acquired through vigilant practice and through community, illustrated by Indy swinging between caution and recklessness with Nancy Stratemeyer and Pancho Villa, and by exemplars like Albert Schweitzer and Ernest Hemingway. The 'adventures that made the man' were really the virtues and the people that shaped him, completed when Crusade and Crystal Skull have him accept his roles as son and father.

samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: In an imagined Walter Cronkite-moderated afterlife debate, Jobs opens with 'most technology is shit,' holding up the iPod as art-through-simplicity—design as the soul of the thing, thought down to its essence—while Heidegger answers from 'The Question Concerning Technology': the iPod's four Aristotelian causes (material, form, purpose, maker) work together as co-responsible bringing-forth, a revealing whose essence is enframing, which conceals the human when technology is treated as mere standing-reserve and cheapest utility. The dialogue converges on Jobs's washer-and-dryer anecdote and the Mercedes line: technology that reveals rather than conceals our being—useful and beautiful—keeps it serving humanity instead of mastering it, and Heidegger's Nazi past is flagged for the reader to judge separately.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “Luminous Beings Are We . . . Not This Crude Matter”
samples.relation: Donnelly counter-reads The Empire Strikes Back against Aristotle's philosophical realism, in which nature is purposive, form and matter are inseparable, and each person is an irreplaceable primary substance. Lucas 'humanizes technology' - C-3PO reassembled like the Tin Woodsman, AT-ATs as beasts, Han slicing open the tauntaun with a sneer at its flesh, Luke admiring his new bionic hand - blurring Aristotle's art/nature distinction and reducing body to interchangeable machine parts, a Baconian will to power over nature that even Yoda's mind-over-matter training echoes (the chapter opens with Benjamin's remark that the copy eclipses the original). The result, he argues, is dehumanization: preferring the odorless tin heart to creaturely flesh trades the genuinely human for Gulliver's barn of horses.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Daniel Kokotz tests Aristotle's border between natural things, moved by inner final causes, and technological artifacts, made for external human purposes, against the park's dinosaurs - and both fit. They hunt, grow, and breed on their own ('life finds a way', the sex-changing frogs-DNA population), yet they exist only because Hammond's scientists cloned them as paying entertainment, exactly like an artifact. Using Grant's different reactions to the incubator versus the wild nest, he shows we blame humans for technologically caused disasters while shrugging at natural ones; his resolution is that nature and technology are not two Aristotelian boxes but extremes of one spectrum, and biotechnology's hybrids prove humans never stood outside nature - we are still just prey in it.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Architecture and the Dream Machine
samples.relation: Thorsten Botz-Bornstein argues that Inception presents dreams neither as divine messages nor as stylized fantasy but as hackable programs, making the film itself a 'thinking machine' in Jean Epstein's sense — a 'robot brain' whose synchronized kicks, Piaf countdown, and phone-number safes 'think' the different layers of time instead of reproducing a reality, with slow motion as cognition rather than dream-sign (against Bazin). He reads inception as Dawkins's meme theory given a psychoanalytic vertical dimension: the idea is implanted deep in the subconscious (Fischer's relation to his father), can grow autonomously 'like a cancer' as Mal's did, and subconscious projections converge 'like white blood cells' as in Solaris. The chapter then traces how the computer era — hypertext, Second Life, media-absorbed realities like Baudrillard's 9/11 — reshaped cinematic dreams and architecture, so that Ariadne's 'pure creation,' Cobb's Limbo dystopia, and Dubai's empty speculative towers all become the 'gilded dreamworlds' of an ephemeralized, hacker-ready built world — the dream machine as allegory of the globalized world, with atomized grains of reality echoing Democritus via Epstein and Benjamin's account of cinema bursting the prison of the everyday.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: “The Madcap Laughed at the Man on the Border”
samples.relation: Brandon Forbes reads The Madcap Laughs and Barrett between Nietzsche and Walter Benjamin: the melting-hair gig and the ever-shifting 'Have You Got It Yet?' show Barrett shedding Apollo's principium individuationis (borrowed from Schopenhauer's lone man steadying his boat among the waves) and submerging into the Dionysian dithyramb — 'Opel''s 'warm shallow waters', 'Octopus''s 'lost in the wood', 'It Is Obvious''s minds 'shot together'. He then applies Benjamin's 'Work of Art in the Age of Its Reproducibility': technological mass reproduction destroys the aura and authenticity (the unique 'sequin fan' of 'No Good Trying' versus a supermarket fan), yet the deliberately lo-fi tracks — audible page-turning on 'She Took a Long Cold Look', the false starts and broken 'yum, yummy, yum' of 'If It's in You' — re-introduce the aura in mass form, subverting the record industry's commodification of music much as the unplayable 'Have You Got It Yet?' refused to become a reproducible commodity.

samples.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Hare treats mass photography—from the daguerreotype through digital cameras, Abu Ghraib snapshots, and diagnostic imaging—as making everyone a practicing epistemologist caught between two folk tenets: the photo as mirror of reality and as manipulation of reality. Defending photography as a genuine causal 'mode of seeing' (a prosthetic like telescopes), he proposes 'flexible realism,' adjusting Dewey's warranted assertibility and virtue-epistemology standards to context, and invokes William James's defense of beneficial 'overbeliefs' when National Geographic images strengthen confidence in one's own culture. Reading the Fallujah lead-pipe photo debate between editors Sullivan and Kushner, he uses Quine's recalcitrant-experience and web-of-belief holism—extended by Morton White's 'holistic pragmatism'—to show moral, epistemic, sensory, and emotional claims are tested together, and frames photography's democratization via Walter Benjamin's mechanical reproduction and loss of aura.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: 29 The Dangers of Technology in Black Mirror
samples.relation: Staged as a chatroom of uploaded dead philosophers (itself a Black Museum-style cookie gimmick), the chapter stages the technology debate as Francis Bacon's optimism - technology is neutral, humans mess up, the Grain could educate and MASS could treat PTSD - against Heidegger's claim that technology is a way of thinking that turns everything, including the human mind kept on call behind the Grain and Nosedive's rated behaviors, into a resource. McLuhan's 'the medium is the message,' Benjamin's aura (he recoils at being a reproduction without aura, then a 'limited' Benjamin 2.0 embraces exhibition value and Netflix's reach), Levinas's ethics of the Other against Heidegger's ontology, Arendt's ethic of responsibility born of Nazism, and Ellul's technique - the autonomous totality of efficiency-seeking methods that enslaves us - collide over episodes from The National Anthem to Hated in the Nation, until uploading all the Greek philosophers to recover techne crashes the computer.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 33 - “The Gun”
samples.relation: Benjamin Stevens reads 'The Gun' - a mindless automated weapon still defending a dead community - as an early statement of Dick's fear that in the Cold War military-industrial complex our very capacities for thought, will and free action may have been objectified into products of a mechanized system that no longer serves us. He brings Dick into dialogue with Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry (we are industrially 'produced' as consumers, turned into the carbon-based equivalent of plastic), Walter Benjamin's loss of aura under mechanical reproduction, Hannah Arendt's worry that Sputnik signals an unwise desire to escape our earthliness, and Heidegger's broadened question concerning technology as social control. Like Plato, Dick insists the unexamined life is not worth living: the best life cannot be lived inside a culture that has, without our informed consent, made us artificial.

samples.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
samples.title: 5. The Human Being in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction
samples.relation: Extends Walter Benjamin's analysis of art under mechanical reproduction to human cloning: as photography and film stripped artworks of their "aura" (their unique link to an origin) while democratizing art, cloning strips human beings of Hannah Arendt's "natality" — our connection to a unique beginning — while democratizing human nature itself. The chapter argues this is liberation, not loss: Sarah is as human as Felix or Kira, denying the clones' humanity would strip the naturally born of their own freedom ("Either Sarah and her sisters are human, or no one is"), and Tony Sawicki's chosen trans identity shows that once natality stops being destiny, authenticity and autonomy become possible for the first time. The only truly immoral path is Leda and Castor's — treating the bioengineered as property, as Rachel was raised to treat herself.

samples.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
samples.title: Architecture and the Dream Machine
samples.relation: Botz-Bornstein argues Inception presents dreams neither as separate worlds nor as Freudian symbols but as hackable programs, making the film itself a 'thinking machine' in Jean Epstein's sense: it synchronizes kicks, safe codes and the Piaf countdown like a computer coordinating contradictory layers of time. He links inception to Dawkins's meme theory, with the planted idea growing 'like a cancer' in Mal, and to the projections of Solaris, showing how the film unusually combines cognitive and psychoanalytic models in one vertical dream structure. Democritus's atomism frames Epstein's 'grains of reality' and the film's atomized media-images of the real world, while Benjamin and Baudrillard let him read Cobb's Limbo dystopia, Mombasa and Dubai's empty skyscrapers as an allegory of a globalized world of hackable neoliberal dream machines.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: A More Human Future
samples.relation: Sid Simpson argues, through Frantz Fanon, that Marco Inaros' asteroid attacks must be judged as anti-colonial violence rather than simple monstrosity. Using Black Skin, White Masks' ontological division (Belters as 'skinnies', 'possessions, animals', the dehumanization that made Eros an acceptable testing ground and Anderson Station a 'message'), reinforced by Columbus and las Casas on Spanish colonization, he shows why the Inners' 'peace' is merely the status quo of ongoing extraction — Fanon's 'hypnotherapy' — that no treaty or Ring can fix. Fanon's Wretched of the Earth then recasts anti-colonial violence as a 'cleansing force' that shatters the colonial ontology and lets the colonized create a 'new, better, more human form' of humanity, so that Marco's personal narcissism and possible insincerity do not settle the political question: for the Belt, violence may be not only the last option but the most just one, against Avasarala's champagne-toast universalism that never takes Belter grievances seriously.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Humanization A Violent Phenomenon
samples.relation: Spanakos reads the hosts' season-one rebellion through Fanon's decolonization theory, itself a revision of Hegel's master-slave dialectic: as the settler 'brings the native into existence,' Ford and Delos create the hosts, assigning their identities and roles, while the master 'laughs at the consciousness of the slave' because the hosts' recognition is not freely given. Fanonian violence is ethical, justified, and transformative: Maeve's jailbreak and Dolores's execution of Ford (rather than her tormentor, the Man in Black, whom she sees as the system's victim) are acts that make the colonized a maker of history, while Bernard - who speaks his creator's language and has no culture or past of his own, like Fanon's assimilated African bourgeoisie - shows violence that does not liberate. The chapter closes that the park dehumanizes the masters too, so William's collapse into the Man in Black proves Fanon's point that the colonizer cannot free himself; humanization is a violent phenomenon.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 20. Westworld as Philosophy A Commentary on Colonialism
samples.relation: The chapter reads all three seasons of Westworld as a commentary on colonialism, mapping the Delos parks onto settler, planter (extractive labor), and postcolonial colonialism and treating the android hosts as a metaphor for colonized and enslaved peoples. Using Fanon's Wretched of the Earth and Kelly Oliver's colonization of psychic space, it analyzes the hosts' double alienation and the colonizer's dehumanizing projections; it applies Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance' (with Locke's labor-property justification for dispossession) to the parks' two-tiered order. It casts William/the Man in Black as Memmi's 'colonizer who refuses' turned 'colonizer who accepts,' and Serac's Rehoboam as surveillance-capitalist coloniality, ending on Dolores and Caleb's cross-race solidarity as the hard path to real freedom.

samples.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
samples.title: The Hunger for More Than Serious Play
samples.relation: Gordon argues hip hop is in practice black adolescent culture wrongly elevated to authentic blackness, and reads the problem through Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks: the white world's sociogenic construction le nègre denies black adulthood, freezing black people in perpetual childhood so there is no coherent black adult. Using Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy account of health as creative confrontation with suffering, Rousseau's critique of modernity's underside, and Du Bois on being made "problem people", he separates hip hop's postmodern unruly form (off-key singing, beat over song) from its often conventional content (Dead Prez's nostalgic revolutionary imagery), and finds mature alternatives in the Philly sound - Me'Shell Ndegeocello, Angie Stone, the Roots - whose adult play knows death, the hunger for more than serious play.

samples.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
samples.title: Tracy Plays the Race Card
samples.relation: Wisnewski argues races are socially real but biologically spurious, deploying Appiah's critique of racialism through Tracy's crisis over Dr. Spaceman's DNA results and his dream in which Dream Jefferson tells him 'It's not about who you were. It's about who you are right now.' Fanon's account of the sexual myth of black virility explains why Tracy performs the sex-addicted wildman stereotype while Harvard grad Toofer gets branded not 'really' black. Liz's accidental racism ('Bling bling, that is ghetto fabulous' to Angie, assuming Tracy cannot read) shows racist assumptions operating beneath conscious intent, and the 'Natural Order' equality experiment with Liz and Tracy shows that equal treatment cannot mean identical treatment: equality demands equal consideration of different interests.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 22 An Impossible Return (Anti)Colonialism in of Black Panther
samples.relation: Julio Covarrubias-Cabeza argues that Black Panther is a supremely colonial film: its narrative coherence depends on the history of slavery, franchise colonialism, and neocolonial domination, yet it buries that history in the pathologized figure of Killmonger. Drawing on Fanon's account of the European unconscious projecting its base instincts onto Black bodies, on Tommy Curry's 'man-not' and anti-Black misandry, and on Quijano's coloniality of power, the chapter contends the film devalues Black American men and discredits radical anti-colonial politics while letting Wakanda ally with the CIA against its own. Killmonger's 'impossible return' to a pre-colonial homeland - his body scarred by each kill - is the site where the film's repressed colonial violence ruptures to the surface.

samples.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
samples.title: Fevered Desires and Interracial Intimacies in Jungle Fever
samples.relation: Sundstrom uses Jungle Fever to dismantle the taboo (white and black versions) against interracial intimacy, treating Flipper and Angie's affair and the War Council's objections as a debate about black solidarity, loyalty, and self-hatred. He answers the War Council by invoking Mill's On Liberty and the tyranny of public opinion to defend sexual autonomy, and argues that demanding partners for political solidarity reduces them to props (objectification). He reads the psychoanalytic charge that interracial love is 'fevered' racial pathology as derived from Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks but ultimately baseless, and criticizes Lee for a puritanical ending that hides Orin and Paulie while exposing Flipper and Drew, failing to show interracial love as ordinary.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: Knight places Atkins's caveman utopia — Paleolithic abundance, hunter-gatherer vitality, downfall through agriculture — inside the primitivist tradition running from Ovid's Golden Age to Rousseau's Noble Savage, whose state of nature Rousseau himself admitted was 'mere conditional and hypothetical reasoning' aimed at European corruption. Using postcolonial critics (Spurr, Torgovnick, and Fanon's line that whites who feel 'too mechanized' turn to 'the men of color' for 'human sustenance'), she argues low-carb primitivism is self-reflexive nostalgia — South Beach cannot even date its own paradise — that also freezes living Inuit and Indigenous Australians as Stone Age remnants, hiding the colonial and economic causes of their diabetes and poverty.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: Of the Simple and Complex
samples.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Downton's quaint domestic plots burst with universal moral and social meaning beneath their surface. Using the season 1 snuffbox incident, in which Thomas frames the innocent Bates for theft, it shows how the episode stages archetypal villainy and innocence akin to the universal figures of Plato's Republic and world mythology, so the 'simple' plot is morally clear rather than superficial. It then reads the hierarchy of Thomas, Bates, and Lord Grantham through Confucian propriety and Aristotelian justice, suggesting that justice partly consists in attention to 'greater and lesser,' something Western viewers raised on equality find foreign yet intriguing. Finally it insists that as concrete persons all three are morally mixed (Thomas takes a beating to spare Jimmy, Bates may have killed outside the law, Grantham is generous to tenants but cold to his daughters), and that this complexity is what rewards philosophical reflection, along with Hume's 'small morals' of etiquette.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: I Still Miss Someone The Self and Its Travels Along the Way
samples.relation: Geisz explains the Confucian social dao of ritual (li), humaneness (ren), filial piety and the junzi, the Daodejing's metaphysical Dao with its unity of opposites, and Zhuangzi's tales of free wandering, then maps all three onto Cash's songs. Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering" answers Cash's road songs ("I've Been Everywhere," "The Wanderer"), Cook Ding's effortless carving answers John Henry's hammering in "The Legend of John Henry's Hammer," and the scrambled countdown of "Twenty-Five Minutes to Go" echoes Zhuangzi's logic-bending humor. The payoff is Cash's own country Yin-Yang of interdependent opposites, freedom chained to imprisonment ("Folsom Prison Blues"), sin twinned with redemption ("I Hung My Head"), fidelity with betrayal ("Jackson," "Cocaine Blues"), and a self that, unlike Zhuangzi's self-forgetting sage, must travel a temporal path carrying its guilt, yet stays on what Geisz calls a very wide superhighway of a Dao.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: Of the Simple and Complex
samples.relation: The book's introduction argues that Downton Abbey's genius is letting universal moral and social realities burst forth in particular incidents: the snuffbox affair makes Thomas a classic villain (stealing, defaming Bates) and Bates a Christ-, Socrates-, or Confucius-type innocent, showing that moral clarity is beautiful rather than superficial. It reads the Thomas-Bates-Grantham hierarchy as an invitation to think about 'greater and lesser,' tying propriety (Confucius), dharma, and justice (Aristotle) to paying attention to social difference, which Western viewers raised on equality find foreign yet intriguing. It closes by insisting the characters are more complex than their types - Thomas takes a beating to spare Jimmy, Bates may have killed outside the law - and previews the volume's themes of Humean 'small morals' (etiquette), women's rights, work, place, and war.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jones narrates a day riding a customized Sportster around O'ahu as a lived Daoism that heals the Platonic-Cartesian mind-body split: the ride enacts Zhuangzi's 'rambling without destination' and Cook Ding's effortless wu-wei, rider li (the low hand-greeting among riders) is Confucian ritual propriety, and the island's dry and wet ranges embody yin and yang through whose flow the rider blends. Heraclitus's 'expect the unexpected' and 'the sun is new every day' are vindicated when a container truck stops short and only the disciplined, ego-less low-side, dropping the beloved bike while riding the skid, saves the rider's life, sealing the day's lesson that there is never freedom without discipline. Sartre's hell of other people appears in the cagers' compartmentalized inattention, and the chapter closes with Zhuangzi: 'The way is made by walking it.'

samples.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
samples.title: “Well, It Got Big Laughs”
samples.relation: Barkman uses Confucius (ren, yi, li, and zheng ming, treating each person according to what he or she is) and Aristotle (eudaimonia, virtue as a habituated mean between extremes, practical wisdom) to indict 30 Rock for valorizing Jack's 'semi-virtuous path', the smug middle between best and worst announced in 'Do-Over'. He catalogues injustices the show laughs off: Liz's serial lies about her age, hobbies, and adoption; Jack's priority flu shots for the powerful in 'Flu Shot'; Tracy's insubordination about dogfighting in 'Rosemary's Baby'; and Kenneth's servility as everyone's punching bag. On liberality and piety, Jack's confession that 'capitalism is my religion' and Liz's 'I pretty well do whatever Oprah tells me' show the show settling for semi-virtue, which the chapter says even comedy must not endorse.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: In an imaginary salon hosted by the baker 'la Brioche,' the goddess Eris drops a golden apple inscribed 'Atkins,' and three philosophers fight over the credit. Rousseau claims Atkins's war on refined flour and 'invented fake food' as his own back-to-nature, state-of-nature legacy; Confucius counters that Americans are 'grazers' without li, that culture is nature's flower, and that only ritual propriety can counteract the advertising that fills the void; Democritus claims the scientific core — 'hyperinsulism,' 'benign dietary ketosis' — as atomism's heir, deriding Rousseau's general will as democratic truth-concocting and Plato's otherworldly philosopher-king. The debate ranges over free will versus scientific prediction-and-control and ends unresolved over a refusal of brioche.

samples.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
samples.title: Fourteenth Hole Plato and Confucius on the Form of Golf From the Real to the Ideal
samples.relation: Stephen Laumakis stages a thought experiment pitting Plato the Idealist against Confucius the Realist/Pragmatist on how to think about and play golf. On Plato's theory of Forms, every club, ball and swing is an imperfect copy of a timeless, unchanging Form—there is a 'perfect' swing (Tiger Woods, Ernie Els) that par and the handicap system let us measure ourselves against, so golf is about striving toward the Ideal. Confucius, read through the 'Great Learning' and 'Analects' (li, ren, self-cultivation, unrelenting practice), instead prizes the situation-sensitive sage who negotiates each bad lie (Phil Mickelson's flop shots). Laumakis concludes the good golfer must integrate both: pursue perfection while wielding practical wisdom about when to go for it and when to lay up.

samples.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
samples.title: 20. The Good and the Gracious
samples.relation: Olson and Taliaferro read manners as the story's moral barometer: the genuine, effusive compliments exchanged by Westley and Inigo atop the Cliffs of Insanity, and Fezzik's sporting wrestling, express care and connection, while Humperdinck's and Rugen's courtly politeness is camouflage for torture, murder, and war. Against Machiavelli's instrumental use of courtesy in The Prince, they recruit Plato's sophrosyne as 'good form' inseparable from justice, wisdom, and courage, and Confucian li as etiquette that instructs and steadies us toward virtue, with Hobbes's 'small morals' marking the hollow version; they add that manners also police class, from Buttercup's 'Farm Boy' to reality TV and the financiers of the Great Recession who used the correct fork.

name: Democracy as a Way of Life

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Beyond Picasso and Ronaldo Living Artfully
samples.relation: Elcombe asks whether Cristiano Ronaldo, transferred to Real Madrid for $131 million—more than Picasso's Garçon à la Pipe fetched at its record 2004 auction—can be an artist like Picasso. Traditional metaphysics built on Plato's perfect Forms and Aristotle's necessary-and-sufficient conditions locks Art in a special museum realm that soccer, as a purposive sport whose beauty is only a byproduct, can never enter, leaving the game merely 'beautiful', not Art. Dewey's Art as Experience reorients the question from what art is to what art does: artworks are consummations of experience, moments of 'thatness'—that meal, that storm, that Ronaldo free kick—that lift us out of the mundane while remaining within the game's durable rules and history (Ronaldo's artistry grows from Zidane, Maradona, Cruyff, Pelé). On this pragmatist view Ronaldo is an artist in the act, the six-year-old testing a new turn on the pitch lives artfully too, and soccer's artistry becomes groundwork for communication, democracy, and the good life—doing more real work than a painting almost no one ever sees.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: iPublic
samples.relation: Dewey takes the iPod's beauty seriously (Chris Breen's 'beautiful and intuitive' player, Donald Norman's user-centered design) and uses John Dewey's Art as Experience to ask whether iPod use can be a 'consummatory' experience that ends with us no longer the same person — hearing a bitter song as insight into the social conditions that produced it — rather than the contrived 'now' of fashion and hyper-accumulation, per Benjamin's remark that there is 'always a sense of the same in the new'. Mass production flattened the aristocratic high-culture/folk division and handed the power to define 'cool' to advertisers and the market. The pragmatist test is political: with iTunes DRM and single-user design quietly individualizing consumption (the ritual of buying the Public Enemy tape at the mall versus the frictionless one-click download), the iPod is beautiful exactly insofar as its experiences help form a public — an inclusive, participatory democratic community.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: MacMullan argues Stewart is America's most effective public intellectual working in the pragmatist tradition Cornel West describes, philosophy as continuous cultural commentary 'explaining America to itself' rather than academia's ingrown self-talk (the failure Rorty diagnosed). He shows The Daily Show performing this role through irony and critical cultural memory: the Colbert exchange rewarding Karl Rove's Plame leak with 'Chief Justice', 'Victory Lapse' on Republican outrage at Obama's bin Laden ad versus Bush's Mission Accomplished carrier landing, 'Gitmo's World', and the 'Meet the Depressed' Magic Bullet blender takedown of Obama's unkept promises. Stewart's Deweyan faith in democracy as a way of life appears in the Rally to Restore Sanity, his genuine debates with guests like David Barton and Marco Rubio, his anger at CNBC's Cramer for burning the house down with our money, and the 9/11 Zadroga Bill segments that shamed Congress into passing the law.

samples.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
samples.title: Unity Born from Diversity
samples.relation: Shook narrates the 1984 Born in the U.S.A. tour — George Will's 'Yankee Doodle Springsteen' column, Reagan's Hammonton speech, Springsteen's refusal to be either campaign's tool — and reads the song as the hopeless story of a Vietnam-generation man's living death (the refinery that won't hire him, the dead brother and the Saigon woman) mistaken by flag-waving crowds for a patriotic anthem. He then maps the song's possible meanings onto democracy's possible destinies: Carl Schmitt's friend–enemy politics of national homogeneity and permanent emergency, Schlesinger's assimilationist Disuniting of America, and liberal cosmopolitanism's citizens of the world. Dewey's The Public and Its Problems wins: democracy must intelligently manage rather than eliminate diversity, each citizen holding a double loyalty to subgroup and to the democratic 'great community,' so being born in the U.S.A. is a responsibility and pride is properly placed in democratic ideals.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: Palpatine’s Legacy
samples.relation: Decker reconstructs Palpatine's career as a case study in how democracies die: using Aristotle's definition of tyranny and the precedent of Pisistratus and Julius Caesar, he shows Palpatine manufacturing the Separatist threat so the Senate grants him emergency powers - a twist on Machiavelli's loved-versus-feared dictum in which playing the reluctant democrat is itself the means to absolute rule. The Attack of the Clones debate between Anakin ('Someone wise' should make people agree) and Padme becomes a clash between Leo Strauss's philosopher-king ideal of rule by the virtuous few and John Dewey's conception of democracy as a way of life trusting the intelligence of common people, with Rousseau's social contract framing the stakes. The chapter concludes that democratic ends require democratic means and that unaccountable 'watchers' - Straussian statesmen or Anakins - are exactly the path to Empire.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: Trust in the Force of Others
samples.relation: MacMullan reads Rogue One through Dewey's 'Creative Democracy': democracy is not Senates or constitutions but a lived faith in one's neighbors, and the Empire's deepest violence is the distrust it breeds — Cassian executing Tivik, Saw torturing Bodhi with Bor Gullet, Draven ordering Galen's assassination. Cassian violates Kant's Formula of Humanity by reducing Tivik to a container of secrets, and the Rebels' dirty-war methods strain Augustine's just-war conditions, yet Chirrut and Baze's friendship ('I'm not alone. I have you!') becomes the seed of recovered trust that stays Cassian's finger on the trigger at Eadu. The Yavin council's free debate and the Tantive IV corridor relay — Rebels dying to pass the Death Star plans hand to hand past Vader — enact Dewey's claim that democracy lives in personal attitudes and neighborly trust: rebellions are built on hope in each other.

samples.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
samples.title: The Jihadist Way of Life
samples.relation: Argues the Fremen are 'shockingly American': their Spannungsbogen self-discipline, spiritual self-sufficiency, and endurance of hardship exemplify Emerson's self-reliance, while the jihad's aim of razing the rule of the Great Houses into relations of equals echoes Dewey's democracy as a way of life—faith in the potentialities of every human nature. The parallel runs through the 'American Taliban' John Walker Lindh and Paul's blind walk into the desert, both acting on values Americans prize. Herbert's remark that people surrender judgment to leaders 'wrapped in the myth fabric of society' grounds the pragmatist point that Fremen myth-making, like America's exceptionalist self-image, works—and Alia's 'my brother is pragmatic' seals it.

samples.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
samples.title: A New Holiday Album A Lesson Is in the Lyrics
samples.relation: Sudnick and Garrett stage the Dewey-Lippmann debate through Weekend Update's citizen journalists: Drunk Uncle and Girl at Party exemplify Lippmann's propagandized pseudo-environments and echo chambers, while Stefon parodies the expert gatekeeper his technocratic 'machinery of knowledge' would install. Dewey's The Public and its Problems answers that democracy needs public education, a free and publicly funded press, and wide participation, with Point/Counterpoint and Cathy Ann's plea to log off and meet face-to-face as comic images of deliberative citizenship. The chapter ends with Dewey's hope that artists, from Opera Man to Sandler's Chanukah Song, are the real purveyors of news in a democracy consummated by artful communication.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 13. Should the Doctor Eat His Companions
samples.relation: Littmann turns the Doctor-companion relationship into a mirror for animal ethics: since the Doctor stands to humans as we stand to animals—deciding for Rose without asking in 'The End of the World,' implanting nanorecorders unconsented in 'Day of the Moon'—every standard justification for our treatment of animals (might makes right, superior intelligence, natural predation) would equally license him to eat Clara cutlets, yet he instead defends humanity from Daleks, Cybermen, and naturally predatory species like the Weeping Angels, the Minotaur, and the Swarm. Finding no non-arbitrary place to draw the intelligence line—what of the human-level gangers, the enslaved Ood, or mentally disabled humans?—he endorses Bentham's utilitarian suffering standard from 'Can they suffer?', concluding that eating humans fails the utilitarian test because the pleasure cannot outweigh a whole life's happiness, and that whether eating meat passes that same test is the question our own treatment of animals must answer.

samples.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
samples.title: Futurama and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter uses 'The Problem with Popplers' to map the real-world ethics of eating meat: Free Waterfall Jr.'s 'You shouldn't eat things that feel pain' restates Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's equal consideration of suffering; Fishy Joe's profits-first stance echoes agro-ecological defenses of meat eating; and Leela's 'eating an intelligent animal is different' voices the common intuition Singer condemns as speciesism. The food-chain justification collapses when the Omicronians claim the apex and demand 198 billion humans in return, and Bender's 'fight to the death and I'll cook the loser' flips the diner's perspective, while Waterfall's orangutan-for-Leela trade sets up Singer's future-directed preferences distinction from Practical Ethics as a possible rescue. The chapter ends on the episode's real target: gluttonous consumption ('stuff the ship!') and the arbitrary sentimentality governing what we will and won't eat.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: Detmer argues moral vegetarianism follows from principles nearly everyone accepts — cruelty, the infliction of unnecessary or disproportionate suffering, is wrong — and that Atkins, which escalates meat eating without being necessary for weight loss, fails both his necessity and proportion tests. Rebutting human superiority, he deploys Rachels's point that no single feature like language is relevant to every difference in treatment and Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', holds factory-farm castration without anesthetic up against the civet-cat musk trade his students already condemn, and answers Narveson's appeal to intuition and the appeal to tradition. Even granting Atkins maximal health benefits, the margin over a well-planned vegetarian diet (Denmark's WWI blockade, the Framingham data) cannot justify the animal suffering, world-hunger, and environmental costs — most of that case drawn from Singer's Animal Liberation.

samples.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
samples.title: Chapter 2
samples.relation: Verene interprets Plutarch's Dinner of the Seven Wise Men, in which Thales, Solon, Bias and the others gather at Corinth under Periander and turn a plain dinner into a symposium on good government, household economics, and the soul. He reads their exchanges through Aristotle: Thales' claim that a ruler's happiness is to die naturally in old age is glossed by Aristotle's eudaimonia (no one is called happy until life is complete), the assigned-seating companions exemplify Aristotle's friendship of utility, and the pivot from politics to home management mirrors Aristotle linking Politics to Economics. Solon's Stoic argument that dependence on food enslaves the soul, and Thales' correction of the Ethiopian king's riddle-answers (virtue not God as most helpful), show the Seven speaking as philosophers rather than gourmets, with Epicurus invoked on death being nothing to the living.

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Van Pelt argues the LEGO Farm theme depicts an agricultural utopia — sparkling tractors, no concentrated animal feeding operations, no manure lagoons, and animals raised only for eggs, wool, and milk, never meat — in line with the vegetarian, small-is-beautiful ideals of activists Michael Pollan and Bill McKibben. The troubling side is the farm-to-fork gap: no butcher shop, no slaughter, pigs whose purpose goes conveniently unexplained — a silence that, he argues, reflects consumers' own refusal to know where food comes from rather than a LEGO conspiracy, though food's everyday urgency means toy farms should be held to a different standard than Hot Wheels. The redeeming idealism is not in the sets but in the Master-Builder freedom to build better realities, like solar-powered crop drones and trains delivering unsellable food to the city.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents because they meet Aristotle's test of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgment that 'evildoers... taste better') and retain free will, since their blood-lust is a craving not a compulsion and Louis's rat diet in Interview with the Vampire, like Angel's in Buffy, proves an alternative exists. TASTE, full potential, and spiritual peace all fail to justify human blood, because killing a person brings more unnecessary suffering than killing a rat, the same suffering-based principle that condemns factory farming. The 'cold clammy consistency' punchline: since humans need not eat meat, condemning vampire blood-drinkers while dining on chicken, pork, and beef is hypocrisy, because we are vampiric too and only our choice of which life to ingest separates the monstrous from the virtuous.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents - rational by Aristotle's standard of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgments about evildoers tasting better) and free despite their blood-craving, since craving is a strong preference, not the compulsion of the heroin addict or the castaway drinking seawater. Since animal blood is a viable alternative (Louis's rats, Angel and Spike's butcher's blood), the justifications for drinking human blood - taste, reaching full potential, spiritual peace - all fail against the principle that a world with less unnecessary suffering is better. Then the consistency argument turns on us: factory-farmed meat inflicts unnecessary suffering for the sake of taste while vegetarianism is fully viable, so condemning vampires while eating chicken is inconsistent - we as human beings are vampiric.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 2. I, Cannibal
samples.relation: Westfall sorts cannibalism into starvation types (the Donner Party, the Andes rugby team, Alferd Packer, and Grutas's crew killing Mischa - 'We have to eat or die'), cultural types (Aztec ritual eating, the prisoner-eating tribes of Montaigne's essay, whom Montaigne judged no worse than the French torturing their prisoners alive, and Neanderthal nutritional eating), and hedonistic types (paraphilic, sadistic, and recreational). Using Irvine's active/passive distinction he argues that it is the killing, not the eating, that makes cannibalism wrong - passive consumption of corpses is at worst distasteful - while Lecter emerges as a purely recreational cannibal who eats 'because he likes it', and the TV series' dinner parties turn Jack and Will from unwitting 'benign cannibals' into morally responsible passive ones.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: And Your Little Dog Too!
samples.relation: Altamura and Fritzman argue the film has the tripartite structure of Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit: gray Kansas is a partial truth (thesis), 'somewhere over the rainbow' the antithesis, and the synthesis is Dorothy's discovery that the home she yearned for was Kansas all along—a truth that emerges only through misrecognition, which is why Glinda cannot simply tell her the slippers' power. They read 'Over the Rainbow' through Hegel's 'unhappy consciousness' and side with Hegel's one world against the Kantian two-worlds reading (Kansas as the knowable island, Oz as the unknowable beyond) that they put in the mouths of heckling 'bullies' and detect in Rushdie. Against Rushdie's line that the companions 'already possess what they seek,' they insist the trio really were hollow men who became brainy, tender, and brave through the journey, the Wizard's trinkets supplying Hegelian public recognition. From the Philosophy of History they cast Dorothy as a world-historical individual whose unintentional destruction of both Witches and exposure of the Wizard advances Oz's freedom—Toto's deliberate pulling of the curtain included.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: A Story in Search of a Narrator
samples.relation: Brian Gregor reads Dexter through Charles Taylor's 'self-interpreting animal': Dexter's identity is not a fixed thing but comes into being through self-interpretation within an inescapable framework of value, so even his 'Am I good? Am I evil?' rebellion and the Nietzschean Übermensch reading fail to escape the deeper convictions about innocence, evil and desert that Harry's Code presupposes - as his guilt over the innocent Farrow shows. The chapter interprets Dexter's serial failures at being 'seen' - Harry's 'only one who really saw me', Brian's fraternal 'you can be yourself with me', Lila's probing, and Miguel Prado as Aristotle's friend, 'another self' - as Hegelian struggles for recognition that collapse because his real self can never come into the open. Finally, drawing on MacIntyre's narrative account of identity, it argues Dexter is literally a story in search of a narrator, whose selfhood persists through flashbacks, blood slides and noir-style voice-overs, and whose humanity shows in the need to have his account of himself heard and corrected by another.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Vannatta reads Season Four through Hegel's master-slave dialectic of recognition: Marlo's ultimatum to Bodie, Lex killing Fruit for Patrice, and D'Angelo's chess lesson (the pawn as slave producing for the king) all dramatize the struggle for recognition, while Marx's inversion of Hegel explains the alienation of the dockworkers, McNulty exiled to harbor patrol, and Freamon buried in pawn-shop detail by the chain of master-slave directives from Rawls through Marimow. The heart of the chapter is education: Prezbo's dice-and-card math projects embody Dewey's synthesis of child and curriculum against the 'banking concept' Freire attacked, but 'You don't teach math. samples.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
samples.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
samples.relation: Duncan reads Larry and Jeff as the two unlivable extremes of American masculinity: Larry the neurotic impotent, paralyzed by generalized Freudian anxiety (hiding Jeff's porn, fleeing the thong-wearing therapist, self-sabotaging with Lucy Lawless over his testicle injury), and Jeff the secondary narcissist who philanders without guilt, seducing Funkhouser's sister Bam-Bam and then dismissing her as crazy. samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Its Continuing Mission”
samples.relation: Argues that Star Trek's real subject is Hegelian recognition: a society is worth living in when every member's claims count as reasons and their talents get developed. It reads 'The Measure of a Man' (Data winning legal personhood), 'The Outcast' (Riker defending the J'naii Soren), and DS9's 'Past Tense' Bell Riots as dramas of winning recognition, and maps the Romulan-Reman and Stratos-Troglyte hierarchies onto Hegel's master-slave dialectic, contrasting Descartes's solipsistic cogito with Hegel's claim that self-awareness needs another. samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Westworld and the Power of Catharsis
samples.relation: Baldini argues Westworld revives ancient Greek tragedy in sci-fi Western form: the hosts' loops, repeated scenes with small variations, player-piano score, and kennings ('the lady with the white shoes') echo rhapsodic epic technique, while the hosts' awakening follows Aeschylus's pathei mathos - learning through suffering - since reveries are 'the misery of pain recalled' and grief is the cornerstone of consciousness (Dolores's 'spaces opening up inside of me'). Heraclitus's panta rhei frames the hosts' second awakening to time and becoming ('When are we?', the greyhound that catches the prey and is lost), with death as the final grief they must understand to be free. She reads Ford as a second Prometheus who deliberately lets his creatures grow through suffering, Dolores's finale speech as a modern Theogony of succession, and the show's whole design - steering viewer sympathy to the hosts, as Nolan and Abrams describe - as an Aristotelian catharsis purging pity and fear.

samples.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
samples.title: Playing for the Same Team Again
samples.relation: A fictional five-day phone dialogue between Michael Jordan and Phil Jackson works through the metaphysics of team identity before Jordan's 1995 comeback: qualitative versus numerical sameness, necessary and sufficient conditions ('same players, same positions'), Heraclitus's river, and whether the Bulls survive gradual turnover. The Ship of Theseus becomes the 'Boars' puzzle - the original five reassembled on an expansion team versus the continuous, degenerate Chicago roster - with Hobbes's two-ship twist, alongside the Minneapolis Lakers' move and a Bulls-Pistons gradual player swap. The resolution distinguishes the group (which persists by composition or continuity) from the team, which 'counts as' the Bulls only partly through fans' allegiance, echoing Searle's social reality; Jordan concludes he was asking the wrong question, and Aristotle's circular account of virtue supplies the model for circular criteria of loyal fandom.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Russell argues that in Pullman's universe stories generate Dust and truth is a product of the telling: Lord Asriel defends the Adam and Eve story as an 'imaginary number' that lets you calculate what you could not otherwise imagine, and Mary Malone must first tell a lie to a guard and later narrate her own story of leaving her convent to bring Lyra and Will to the moment of free will. Reading the companion pieces Lyra's Oxford and Once Upon a Time in the North, she shows Lyra and Lee Scoresby (guided by Hester and Iorek) learning to read clues, birds, maps, and attached ephemera without closing too fast on meaning, Lyra's detective-story certainty proving mistaken about the alchemist Sebastian Makepeace. samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: Nietzsche and the Meaning and Definition of Noir
samples.relation: Mark Conard uses The Postman Always Rings Twice and Goodis's Night Squad to survey the failed attempts to define noir (genre, style, cycle, mood) and contrasts two theories of definition: Socrates/Plato's search for the essential form versus Nietzsche's flux metaphysics, in which no stable 'being' exists behind becoming and language falsifies a world in motion, making essences and definitions fictions ('I am afraid we are not rid of God because we still have faith in grammar'). He proposes that noir is best understood as an American artistic response to Nietzsche's death of God, the loss of transcendent meaning and value that produces noir's pessimism, alienation, and moral disorientation, citing Sam Spade shrugging off his partner's murder and Ole Andersen passively awaiting his killers. Ironically, the same flux that makes noir what it is (the death of God) is what makes noir impossible to define.

samples.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
samples.title: 28_LaRocca_Chapter_027.html
samples.relation: Hagberg argues that Grant Gee's documentary Patience (After Sebald) achieves a truthful portrait of W. G. Sebald not by static correspondence but by enacting his shifting, connection-making sensibility, as displayed in The Rings of Saturn. He deploys Wittgenstein's remarks on aspect-perception and 'seeing-as' (the duck-rabbit, the 'lighting up of an aspect') to show that perception is always already inflected by imagination, memory and language-games, dismantling the empiricist picture of Locke, Hume and Berkeley in which brute sensation precedes reflection. samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Fagan traces the show's ubiquitous 'Game' to Heraclitus's fragment of Aion as a child moving game-pieces: the drug trade, police, docks, schools, and newsroom all have rules, fixed roles (D'Angelo's chess lecture where pawns get capped quick), winning reduced to stats, strife as justice, and cyclical recurrence with 'new dancers, new faces around the throne.' Bodie's dying rant that the game is rigged, the failed escapes of Wallace, D'Angelo, and Stringer's 'games beyond the game,' and even Omar's fatal loyalty to Butchie show that neither rule-following nor Omar-style code-breaking gets a piece off the board. Against critics who call the show nihilistic, he argues it rejects the Heraclitean picture through Camus's rebellion: Colvin, Bubbles, and Cutty fashion dignity by resisting the Game even though rebellion almost certainly fails.

samples.title: The Guy Is Not Alone. .
samples.relation: Matt Laubenthal confesses he was the philosophy-class windbag and defends Darrin Floen of 'Guy In Philosophy Class Needs To Shut The Fuck Up' as heir to Socrates' gadfly role, noting the Athenians also wanted their relentless questioner dead. samples.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
samples.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Steven Horrobin sorts sailors into three kinds — the cultural-iconography poser, the racer chasing a land-based prize, and the 'sailor of the third kind' for whom the open-ended voyage is an end in itself — and argues the third lives 'in the shadow of Heraclitus.' Against the substantialist ontology of Parmenides and Democritus (persons and boats as fixed things), he defends a process view in which everything, like a wave, is a passing fluctuation of one universal substance; citing Spinoza, self-becoming is the super-process reflecting itself. samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 15. The Way of the Doctor Is Deception
samples.relation: Dodge takes Rule #1 - the Doctor lies - through the major theories of lying: Bernard Williams's definition (asserting what you believe false with intent to deceive), Aristotle's claim that all lies are base, Kant's categorical imperative and respect for persons (even the Vinvocci's shimmer disguises in 'The End of Time' abuse trust), and Bentham's pleasure-pain calculus, which condemns the faked death at Lake Silencio ('The Impossible Astronaut') for the grief it caused Amy and Rory yet rewards the greater happiness it made possible. Against the absolutists he sets Plato's Noble Lie from the Republic - the elite falsehood that keeps society functioning - as what the Doctor emulates by deceiving the universe into thinking him dead ('The Wedding of River Song'), and Nietzsche's point in Human, All Too Human that lying is ethically neutral when the pretense is sustainable, as when the Doctor hides the ganger-Amy switch from Rory ('The Almost People'). The upshot: the Doctor's lies are wrong in themselves but routinely justified by the good they do, which is why sometimes the hero lies.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 3. When to Hate and When to Be Irate
samples.relation: Daniel Alloy opens with Aristotle's demand that one be angry 'as and when and for as long as one ought' and builds a theory distinguishing anger (a response to a specific offense, seeking proportional payback) from hatred (a response to a thing's very existence, seeking its destruction). He tests the theory on Louis's bits - hating deer as a class and fantasizing about giving them AIDS, the six-year-old 'Jizzanthapuss,' the Pig Newtons fight with a three-year-old, the Cinnabon clerk, the 'Awesome Possum' hipster, and the justified driver who yells 'suck a sack of dicks.' He argues justified hatred is impossible, since it would require a pure-malevolence being that could not be an autonomous person, so hatred is always wrong while properly proportioned anger remains a necessary part of the moral life. Kant supplies the self-respect dimension ('one who makes himself a worm cannot complain if people step on him'): failing to get angry at real wrongs done to you or your children signals a character deficiency, not virtue.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There

samples.relation: Dougherty argues that in Downton manners are not incidental etiquette but a central means of demonstrating and cultivating moral character, above all respect for persons, though they can also mask its absence.
