The chapter anchors this in Aristotle's person of visible virtue, Nancy Sherman's 'aesthetic of character,' and Sarah Buss's claim that manners constantly remind us that others are worthy of respect, while Sir Richard's boorishness and the Dowager Countess's weaponized courtesy show manners failing or serving self-interest. Mrs. Crawley's etiquette-breaking kindness, praised even by Violet, complicates the picture by showing care can be morally outrun by propriety.

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems

samples.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
samples.title: 14. Of Course It Sucks—It’s Work
samples.relation: Wible stages three theories of work against Dilbert strips: the Greek view of Plato and Aristotle that labor is freedom-sapping and leisure is the civilized ideal, Marx's capitalist critique in which workers become objects and machines (Wally gives off no human vibe, and robots are coming for the engineers), and Desjardins's human-fulfillment model built on Schumacher's creativity, challenge, development, honesty, and beauty, with Wells Fargo's fake accounts showing how jobs that force lying corrupt character. He endorses instead a Kantian middle ground anchored in Norman Bowie's moral minimum: never treating workers as mere means, so the CEO making intern Asok drink industrial sludge on stage is a violation of respect for persons, not just bad management. Sisyphus supplies the image of pointless labor, though even he might be redeemed if he loved the rock.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a12.xhtml
samples.relation: O'Hara argues that play is what makes hobbits - and us - fully human: Bilbo's childhood games of throwing stones, riddles and smoke-rings turn out to be training for the quest (his stone-throwing fells the spiders, his riddle-practice buys time with Gollum), and even Gollum's riddle-game makes him momentarily 'less a monster and more a person'. Following Schiller's and Huizinga's Homo ludens thesis that play completes humanity, he distinguishes play from idleness (Aquinas held recreation continues in heaven; Peirce called play 'vigorous exercise'), places leisure among the goods of Aristotle's 'we play in order to be serious', and contrasts Gandalf's beauty-directed fireworks with the orcs' merely useful explosions and work-chants. But play has limits: Kant warns against treating persons as toys, and Bilbo's lesson is 'Never laugh at live dragons!'

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 18. The Virtues of Choosing Your Faction
samples.relation: Pascoe contrasts Aristotle's and Kant's theories of virtue through the Choosing Ceremony. On Aristotle's account virtues are taught (intellectual) and then habituated into character (moral), tied to one's function, so Susan flourishes because aptitude, upbringing, and choice align while the transfer Al withers - but Tris, Divergent with multiple aptitudes, needs Kant instead: natural virtues are mere 'gifts of nature' that become good only through good will, and her perfect duties to herself and imperfect duties regarding family and faction can justify choosing Dauntless over staying in Abnegation. Kant wins the day: because a corrupted community like Eric's Dauntless redefines bravery into obedience, Tris must think for herself - 'maybe I am wired like the Divergent' - choosing her virtues out of duty and self-respect rather than inheriting them.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bateman replies to Cogburn by recovering the alignment system's actual literary source: Moorcock's Elric saga, where Law and Chaos are rival political ideologies (conservative and liberal tendencies) held in check by the Cosmic Balance, so a Chaotic person need only refuse law's authority, not will horror, and Chaotic Good remains possible. He rejects Cogburn's 'sausage machine' reading of Kant's first formula in favor of the humanity formula and the Realm of Ends, and rejects act utilitarianism as a model of the Good alignment, since an overpopulation scenario shows Mill's calculus mandating culling-genocide and Bentham's felicific calculus cannot actually measure goodness. Drawing on Badiou's ethic of truths, Buddhist and Jain renunciation, and the true-Neutral Druid as servant of the Cosmic Balance, he argues neutrality between Good and Evil need not be monstrous and mourns 4e's 'childishly simplistic' new system.

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 15. Tell the Truth at All Costs
samples.relation: Bowman argues Candor is the most philosophically important faction because its absolute honesty is Kant's ethics: truthfulness as a perfect duty grounded in free will, making even politeness 'deception in pretty packaging,' and forbidding a lie even when the Erudite come to Merciless Mart hunting Tris - which mirrors Kant's reply to Benjamin Constant that one must not lie even to the murderer at the door. Against this he sets Aristotle's virtue ethics, where truth bows to wisdom, justice, and fortitude when the choice is handing hidden Jews to the SS, and Bentham's utilitarianism, which Amity enacts when it lies at the gates to keep the peace and save lives. The Candor Manifesto's 'web of individual-to-individual relationships' and Kant's kingdom of ends explain why universal honesty alone could make truth safe - and why Christina, the Candor, is the one left standing when the city's deception finally destroys it.

samples.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
samples.title: Check Out Time
samples.relation: McGrath and Tilahun ask whether hip hop is bad for women, setting protest and sex-positive tracks (Tupac's "Brenda's Got a Baby", Missy's "One Minute Man", Queen Latifah's "Ladies First", Ms. Dynamite) against endorsements of violence (N.W.A's "One Less Bitch", Snoop's "Can You Control Yo Ho?", 50 Cent's "P.I.M.P"). They apply Mill's harm principle - offend yes, harm no - Hume's counterfactual analysis of causation (the Derek Fisher shot case) to show that whether lyrics cause violence is an unsettled empirical question, Austin and Rae Langton's speech-act theory to argue rappers' cultural authority may let pimp lyrics subordinate women in a way pornography cannot, and Kant's kingdom of ends to charge misogynist lyrics with treating women as mere means.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: From Cash to Kant—and Back Again
samples.relation: Yolanda Estes pairs Cash with Kant as two duty-based moralists: Cash's Golden Rule in 'The Preacher Said, Jesus Said' parallels Kant's formula of humanity (never treating persons merely as means), and Cash's 'good heart' matches Kant's good will, since songs like 'Sam Hall,' 'Folsom Prison Blues' (the man shot in Reno 'just to watch him die'), and 'I Hung My Head' weigh inner motives over outcomes. Because earthly law never balances the moral scale, she reads Kant's kingdom of ends and Cash's apocalyptic kingdom of God in 'When the Man Comes Around' and 'God's Gonna Cut You Down' as parallel objects of faith: we must live as if perfect justice already prevails, working to improve this world rather than waiting for the next.

samples.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
samples.title: Power and Glory Tests of Virtue
samples.relation: The chapter's thesis is that superhero ethics is not utilitarianism (whose perverse 'evil twin' governs Marvel villains) but personalism - the tradition from Borden Parker Bowne to Martin Buber, rooted in Kant's insistence that every person be treated as an end and never merely as a means, and aiming at his 'kingdom of ends'. Heroes who refuse to weigh one innocent against the many enact personalism, and it redeems even Galactus: lying defeated, he is saved by Captain America's and Reed Richards' insistence that 'We had no choice, Galactus', which wins the devourer into a moral community. The authors read the whole arc as the ancient warning against hubris retold in contemporary storytelling.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Architecture and the Dream Machine
samples.relation: Thorsten Botz-Bornstein argues that Inception presents dreams neither as divine messages nor as stylized fantasy but as hackable programs, making the film itself a 'thinking machine' in Jean Epstein's sense — a 'robot brain' whose synchronized kicks, Piaf countdown, and phone-number safes 'think' the different layers of time instead of reproducing a reality, with slow motion as cognition rather than dream-sign (against Bazin). He reads inception as Dawkins's meme theory given a psychoanalytic vertical dimension: the idea is implanted deep in the subconscious (Fischer's relation to his father), can grow autonomously 'like a cancer' as Mal's did, and subconscious projections converge 'like white blood cells' as in Solaris. The chapter then traces how the computer era — hypertext, Second Life, media-absorbed realities like Baudrillard's 9/11 — reshaped cinematic dreams and architecture, so that Ariadne's 'pure creation,' Cobb's Limbo dystopia, and Dubai's empty speculative towers all become the 'gilded dreamworlds' of an ephemeralized, hacker-ready built world — the dream machine as allegory of the globalized world, with atomized grains of reality echoing Democritus via Epstein and Benjamin's account of cinema bursting the prison of the everyday.

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Peter Stone applies Dawkins's memetics and Dennett's Breaking the Spell to the rise of 'Hallelujah' from the troubled release of Various Positions to ubiquity via John Cale, Jeff Buckley, Shrek, and Rufus Wainwright. On Dennett's account religious memes thrive through hyperactive agency detection, doctrines rendered unfalsifiable and thus immune to evidence, and 'belief in belief' - and 'Hallelujah' is religiously ambiguous enough, from David and Bathsheba to Buckley's 'hallelujah of the orgasm,' to be as religious as any singer or congregation wants it to be, whether as Rabbi Kagan's hymn of the heretic or the Holy Trinity Church's 'Amazing Grace' lyric swap. Machiavelli's maxim that fortune governs half the outcome frames the song's lucky trajectory, and its carefully engineered ambiguity makes it a set of very 'happy memes' likely to keep replicating.

samples.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
samples.title: Architecture and the Dream Machine
samples.relation: Botz-Bornstein argues Inception presents dreams neither as separate worlds nor as Freudian symbols but as hackable programs, making the film itself a 'thinking machine' in Jean Epstein's sense: it synchronizes kicks, safe codes and the Piaf countdown like a computer coordinating contradictory layers of time. He links inception to Dawkins's meme theory, with the planted idea growing 'like a cancer' in Mal, and to the projections of Solaris, showing how the film unusually combines cognitive and psychoanalytic models in one vertical dream structure. Democritus's atomism frames Epstein's 'grains of reality' and the film's atomized media-images of the real world, while Benjamin and Baudrillard let him read Cobb's Limbo dystopia, Mombasa and Dubai's empty skyscrapers as an allegory of a globalized world of hackable neoliberal dream machines.

samples.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
samples.title: The Scheme of the Meme
samples.relation: Defining the meme via the OED and Richard Dawkins - a cultural element spread by imitation that mutates like a gene under selection - O'Neil explains why heroes transform: creators get new ideas, markets demand new stories, authors age, new writers arrive, popularity wanes, or an executive has a brainstorm. The evidence ranges over Superman escalating from leaping tall buildings to near-light speed, Batman morphing from 1930s gentleman crime-fighter to Adam West comedian to dark avenger, radio adding Jimmy Olsen and Kryptonite, the Hulk changing color, and Green Lantern changing identity from Alan Scott to Hal Jordan to Kyle Rayner. Gradual change feels organic; the returning fan simply finds the evolved meme unrecognizable.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Shea stages the Wu-Malcolm dispute through Hume's Dialogues: Jurassic Park is an 'intelligent design' so botched that, like Philo's world of needless suffering, it points to ignorant or malicious designers rather than a perfect God, undercutting Richard Owen-style design arguments. He then explains Hammond's folly with Darwinian natural selection and memetics, treating the dinosaur-theme-park as a meme that infected InGen's investors by exploiting evolved desires for profit, fame, and importance. Hammond's fatal errors were assuming evolution 'wants' humans to survive, that complexity means better adapted, and that he could outsmart selection, which the all-female raptors breeding and life 'finding a way' quickly refute.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Don Fallis starts from Joffrey's lie about Arya and the butcher boy Mycah - which costs Mycah's life and Sansa's direwolf Lady's - to dissect lying versus other deception in Westeros: Catelyn accusing Tyrion is not lying because she believes it, Ned's coerced confession at the Great Sept is a real lie (Austin's duress excuse fails, as Thomas More's counterexample shows), and Ned's silence about Joffrey's parentage before the dying Robert is deception by withholding that he himself mistakes for lying. He asks whether lying is morally worse than misleading - Kant and Chisholm say yes, Williams and Scanlon no - testing breach of invited trust (Mirri Maz Duur's 'only death may pay for life'), responsibility-shifting to the audience ('That was a lie you told yourself'), and preserved autonomy (Kant's Groundwork, Mill's On Liberty). Finally, is it worse to lie to a king? Consequentialism explains the danger of misleading the powerful, oaths of fealty and divine right suggest a special duty, but Locke's demolition of divine right (seconded by Monty Python) leaves only the punishment, not the wrongdoing, greater.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Nys asks whether political correctness is a genuine moral demand or mere verbal hygiene, using the British Office: Gareth's racist BMC joke, Brent aborting it when Oliver the Black coworker arrives, the 'wanking claw' impression, and the porn email with Brent's head pasted onto a woman's body. He argues words genuinely wound (Brent's 'sticks and stones' rehearsal collapses when Gareth reveals his cruel nicknames) but that offense is wrong as disrespect for human equality rather than as a feeling, an account filled out with Frankfurt's claim that our identity depends on what we care about, so the non-targeted can be offended too. After weighing Mill's defense of free discussion for social progress, the pornography debate (in which reduction to body parts is exactly what degrades, as Brent complains he was 'objectified'), and Marx's notion of ideology as a concealing set of ideas behind a 'white male' bias, he concludes that Brent's flaw is looking good rather than being good, and that PC language is rhetorical make-up over persisting inequality.

samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy

samples.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits

samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy

The answer comes through Nietzsche's Three Metamorphoses: Asriel, Will, and Lyra play the lion that slays the great 'thou shalt' of the Authority, but the lion's destruction is only the possibility of freedom, since full freedom is Nietzsche's child creating its own values rather than lapsing into nihilism or Sartrean bad faith. samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Challenges the received libertarian message of 'Medicinal Fried Chicken' — Randy giving himself testicular cancer for a marijuana prescription, Cartman bootlegging KFC in a Scarface parody after Colorado bans fast food — by pressing Mill's liberty principle on what 'harm' means: Mr. Garrison's plot to murder the Queer Eye cast is immediate harm, but the S&M Mr. Slave displays to schoolchildren in 'The Death Camp of Tolerance' is only indirect, psychologically mediated harm Mill cannot clearly handle. samples.title: The Gathering of the Tribe Ironic Sacramentalism
samples.relation: Horace Fairlamb argues the Grateful Dead were the Sixties' real revolutionary success: where the New Left failed by keeping confrontational politics, the Dead changed consciousness first, extending Mill's liberal 'experiments in living' into a whole alternative culture. samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: John Henry, the Steam-Engine, and Folsom Prisoners
samples.relation: Mulnix pairs Cash with John Stuart Mill on the priority of quality of life over mere life: Mill's 1868 Parliament speech defends capital punishment as more humane than the "living tomb" of life imprisonment, and Cash agrees in the Folsom liner notes (the prisoner envying the cockroach that can leave) and in "The Mercy Seat," where the electric chair becomes both mercy and the throne of God. Mill's higher and lower pleasures, competent judges, and On Liberty's individuality illuminate Cash's gallery of fools, the "Folsom Prison Blues" narrator who shot a man just to watch him die, the mother-defying Billy Joe of "Don't Take Your Guns to Town," characters whose unreflective rebellion squanders rational freedom. samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: It’s Life in the Solar System, Jim, But Not as We Know It
samples.relation: Uses MacIntyre's demand for self-knowledge — awareness of the social and political currents that shape one's beliefs — to diagnose the Martian Congressional Republic's exceptionalism (Lopez berating 'short-sighted and selfish' Earthers from the Donnager) and to chart Bobbie Draper's redemption arc: refusing to fire first on Ganymede, refusing to bear false witness after the hearings, protecting Holden at the Ring Station, defecting to Avasarala, and finally rescuing Naomi. It maps MCR culture onto American space culture — Kennedy's Rice speech, the Mars Society and National Space Society founding statements, Zubrin's Case for Mars, and Patricia Limerick's and Linda Billings's critique of the 'conquering the space frontier' metaphor, with Carnap's frameworks and Kuhn's incommensurability explaining how metaphors hide alternatives — and argues the MCR never acquires self-knowledge, a failure that ends in its alliance with Marco Inaros and the move to Laconia, while Draper's willingness to update her beliefs shows what philosophy asks of real spaceflight advocates.

samples.book: 025 - The Beatles and Philosophy - Nothing You Can Think that Can't Be Thunk
samples.title: CHAPTER 3 “LOOKING FOR THE INNER HEAT”
samples.relation: The chapter reads Dylan's self-becoming as a chain of identity-emulations and overcomings — Hank Williams, Woody Guthrie, Ramblin' Jack Elliott — with Jon Pankake's folk-police critique and the Mike Seeger epiphany acting as Kuhnian anomalies that force a paradigm shift from folksinger to songwriter, each gatekeeper playing the 'Hegelian negative' Dylan needed. It argues Dylan fused folk, beat poetry, and rock and roll into an 'archaic revival' of mythic, enchanted consciousness against modern rationalization, rejecting the Sartrean/beat existentialism of a meaningless world in favor of co-creating meaning, and treating authenticity as the refusal of fixed identity (the Zimmerman-to-Dylan renaming, 'I'm gonna get me a new Bob Dylan'). The Newsweek exposé, Irwin Silber's open letter, and Johnny Cash's guitar-gift blessing stage his passage from 'King of Folk' to electric rock, with the little-known 1962 cut of Presley's 'That's All Right' showing that going electric was a return home — folk having been, in Dylan's words, 'just an interruption.'

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!

samples.relation: Johnson uses 'Go God Go's' future of 2546—where Dawkins-style atheism has become a warring religion and otter scientists intone 'Oh my Science!'—to ask whether science and religion genuinely conflict and whether New Atheism is itself a faith. Applying abduction and the four criteria of adequacy, he argues the embellished-story hypothesis beats miracle claims about Jesus (whose legend grew Gospel by Gospel), Sathya Sai Baba, Joseph Smith, and Xenu, that Mr(s). Garrison's 'you can't disprove God' and the show's sarcasm commit an appeal to ignorance, and that Stan's water-into-wine scene with Jesus shows how easily people are fooled. He allows Kuhnian theory change in science but rejects James's will-to-believe for existence claims—the moon whale Willzyx needs evidence—and concludes Parker and Stone are unfair to Dawkins: ending religion would not end violence, but it would remove the easiest justification for it, and some answers are simply true even when unknown.

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: Wittgenstein Ultimate Bullshit Detector—or Bullshitter
samples.relation: Fuller argues that mastering a discipline converts critics into loyal insiders — Thomas Kuhn's 'normal science' enshrines the tendency, cognitive dissonance explains it, and Blaise Pascal's wager is the general model of betting on a way of life that makes you receptive to its confirming signs. Against this he sets the Protestant tradition of Luther's conscience, 'playing it by ear', which like the Sophists concedes that reality rarely yields yes-or-no answers — the gap we fill being bullshit — and he frames the dispute as realism versus antirealism, reading Frankfurt's On Bullshit as an ad hominem attack on antirealists. He then re-examines Frankfurt's star witness: Wittgenstein's rebuke of Fania Pascal for saying she felt 'like a dog that has been run over' now looks like a spectacular lack of imagination, since evolutionary psychology, being forged at that very moment, has been narrowing the human-animal mental gap ever since.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Russ Hamer takes Mac's 'Science Is a Liar Sometimes' defense - Aristotle, Galileo, and Newton each proved his predecessor 'a bitch' - and his claim that believing in evolution takes as much faith as belief in God, and answers with philosophy of science. Popper's falsificationism explains why Mac's 'I won't change my mind... regardless of the facts' is the essence of the non-scientific: only theories risking precise, falsifiable predictions (Einstein's light deflection) count as science, unlike vague astrology or Charlie's cherry-picked evidence that the Waitress will love him. Kuhn's distinction of normal and revolutionary science explains why past failures never discredited science - falsifications within a paradigm are tuning, and the Gang's group-configuration trials in 'The Gang Solves the Gas Crisis' are normal science at its best - so revisability is science's strength, not a reason to fear looking like a science bitch.

samples.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
samples.title: Vertigo and Epistemological Vertigo
samples.relation: Flory reads Vertigo as an epistemological parable: Scottie's 'hardheaded Scot' method, collecting facts and deducing from universal principles, fails three times (the step-stool 'cure' for his acrophobia, explaining away Madeleine's 'possession' with the horse statue, forcing Judy up the bell tower for confirmation), delivering an implicit critique of Vienna Circle positivism in the manner of Carnap and Ayer. Against Scottie, the chapter mobilizes Kuhn's theory-laden facts, Aristotle's point that human conduct resists codification by exceptionless laws, and Hume's 'slave of the passions,' with Descartes's automata and Chalmers's philosophical zombies framing the problem of other minds. Midge, who knows people emotionally as well as factually, models the alternative: philosophers who fear 'epistemological vertigo' should give up epistemological training wheels and accept that minds, especially emotions, escape law-like rules.

samples.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
samples.title: 20. The Intersection of Science and Philosophy, the Seediest Corner in Ankh-Morpork
samples.relation: A comic sprint through Western thought anchored in the Science of Discworld books, the chapter runs from Aristotle—whose geocentric four-element physics, it notes, fits Discworld better than Roundworld, and whose condemnations of usury it digresses over—through Descartes's cogito and mind-body dualism, Ryle's 'ghost in the machine,' behaviorism, identity theory, eliminative materialism, and functionalism's brain-as-computer picture, to show how philosophy of mind advances by each theory picking on its predecessor. Newton's occult-seeming gravity, later overturned by Einstein, illustrates the chapter's real thesis drawn from Pratchett's 'Lies-to-Wizards': neither science nor philosophy erects a timeless edifice of facts, since 'every so often, you have to unlearn what you thought you already knew,' while Diogenes and the Cynics supply the model of philosophy done in the common tongue that Pratchett shares.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Thematic Synchronicity
samples.relation: Jones asks what the famous Dark Side of the Rainbow synchronization (album plus The Wizard of Oz, started on the third MGM lion roar) could mean given that the band denies designing it. He catalogs vivid syncs ('Time''s chimes as Miss Gulch bicycles past, 'Money''s cash register entering Munchkinland, 'Us and Them''s 'black and blue' over the Witch and Dorothy), then rejects both the Waters-conspiracy model and Jung's acausal 'synchronicity' as pseudoscience, proposing instead Conrad's apophenia and Kuhn's point that suspecting patterns others miss is the lifeblood of discovery. His resolution is 'thematic synchronicity': both works stage the struggle between security and transcendence, Dorothy's 'Over the Rainbow' against 'Eclipse''s 'all you touch and all you see is all your life will ever be,' so the coincidences feel objective because they are subjectively real to everyone.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Silcox and Cox read D&D modules as thought experiments in James Robert Brown's 'laboratory of the mind'. The Tomb of Horrors' four overlapping plane-shifted buildings restate Parfit's teletransporter puzzle — did the character who stepped through get annihilated, or is an exact copy walking around elsewhere, and does the answer differ for a Warforged or Tiefling? — while the Eberron setting's magically sentient Warforged run into Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?': players cannot access Warforged experience and are really exploring what it is like for a human to suspend disbelief, like Greek actors donning masks. Mary Anne Warren's Space Traveler criteria for alien personhood collapse on contact with orcs who pass them yet eat you, and with the Flumph — lawful good, rational, but killed on sight by the authors' own party — showing personhood cannot be the only criterion for how to treat strangers; the closing twist is that philosophy contemplates scenarios sub specie aeternitatis while D&D forces immersion sub specie temporis, a habit of entertaining the impossible that is itself a philosophical virtue.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: A Dilemma
samples.relation: The chapter asks 'Is your cookie you?', running theories of personal identity through Black Mirror's copies: the soul theory surfaces when Clayton signs away his 'digital self'; Locke's memory theory implies Cookie-Greta is Greta - a reductio, since one person cannot be wholly in two places at once (the same problem for Ashley Too and the thousand Hang the DJ simulations) - and the perdurantist patch recasts Greta and her cookie as time-slices of one four-dimensional person. Physical theories (Olson's animalism, Unger's brain-essentialism) rule out survival by upload, so Yorkie dies when her body dies even though digital Yorkie continues in San Junipero; Parfit's no-self bundle view and the teletransporter case then dissolve the fear, since there is no ego to lose and ordinary survival is 'about as bad' as being destroyed and replaced by a replica. The upshot: the punishment and immortality plots (Joe's million-year Christmas loop, San Junipero) require cookies to be both conscious and psychologically connected in the right way, and the episodes' horror depends on leaving that genuinely uncertain.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Epilog-Rolling
samples.relation: Patton turns the Tin Woodman's backstory—the enchanted axe that costs Nick Chopper his legs, arms, torso and heart, then his head, each replaced by the tinsmith—into a cyborg thought experiment about how much of a person can be swapped out before the person is gone. After a framing nod to Plato's Republic on censoring frightening tales (his father's ban on 'mental violence' fantasy), he brings in Derek Parfit: the R-relation, the 'My Division' brain-split, and the Branch-Line teletransportation case are mapped onto the Woodman (including a hypothetical straw-bodied second Nick) to argue that survival gets different answers from first-person and third-person perspectives. The closing wildcat episode, where the tinned Woodman neatly decapitates a wildcat to save a field mouse, is offered as textual evidence that the tin head failed to preserve moral consistency—so the original Nick Chopper is gone for good, and the Scarecrow's shared brain explains why the two friends later refuse to part.

samples.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
samples.title: P A R T T H R E E
samples.relation: James DiGiovanna uses Dr. Manhattan's origin — disintegration in the intrinsic field chamber and self-reassembly — plus his teleportations to Mars and his split into three simultaneous selves, to run the classic personal identity debates. Descartes's immaterial thinking substance, Hume's mere bundle of perceptions, and Locke's memory theory are tested against a being who remembers in both time directions and rebuilds his body from pure thought ('restructuring myself after the subtraction of my intrinsic field was the first trick I learned'); Parfit's teletransporter, physical and psychological criteria, and fission cases — mirrored in Nagel's split-brain patients — then show ordinary people cannot say whether they would survive teleporting or bisection. The chapter concludes Dr. Manhattan is the only being with fully secure identity, since his consciousness needs neither body nor an unbroken spatiotemporal path and he can encompass several points of view at once.

samples.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Silcox and Cox present D&D modules as thought experiments in James Robert Brown's 'laboratory of the mind': the Tomb of Horrors' plane-shifting doorway forces Parfit's teletransporter question of whether the character who emerges is you, a copy, or an annihilation, extended to Tieflings and Warforged; Eberron's sentient Warforged raise Nagel's bat problem of whether a human player can know what it is like to be a machine, answered with the conclusion that players really explore human pretense, like Greek actors in masks. Mary Anne Warren's Space Traveler criteria for alien personhood strain against orcs who meet them yet attack on sight, and against the players who killed the lawful-good Flumph without parley. The deep difference is perspective: philosophy imagines sub specie aeternitatis while D&D demands immersion sub specie temporis, which nonetheless cultivates the open-minded intellectual virtues philosophers prize.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 5. The One, the Only, Darrow
samples.relation: Kevin McCain uses Darrow's transformations—Helldiver of Lykos, carved Gold lancer, Reaper of Mars—to ask what makes him numerically the same person, warming up with Plutarch's Ship of Theseus replayed on the Pax and the Quinn trading parts. Same-matter and animalist views (Eric Olson) struggle with Mickey's near-total carving and Darrow's restarted heart, and Locke's prince-and-cobbler example, run as a carver swapping Darrow's and the Jackal's psychologies, sinks all physical-continuity views. The simple memory theory breaks transitivity across Darrow's childhood, and Sydney Shoemaker's psychological-continuity fix then fails when a carver splits Darrow's brain into two surviving bodies—a fission case where both new Darrows continue him—while the soul view cannot be verified; the chapter ends with Trenton Merricks's suggestion that there may be no criteria of identity over time at all.

samples.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
samples.title: 12. Becoming Vetinari Personal Identity on the Discworld
samples.relation: Pierce uses Moist von Lipwig's rehabilitation (Albert Spangler becomes Postmaster General), Cosmo Lavish's doomed project of literally becoming Vetinari, the Auditor Myria LeJean, Angua's transformations, the Librarian's orangutan body, Miss Level's two bodies, and duplicated Rincewind teleportation cases to test theories of personal identity. Locke's memory theory, patched by Leibniz into psychological continuity, collapses into circularity under false-memory cases like a wizard implanting Teatime's murders in Rincewind's mind, while bodily and brain-continuity views founder on Igor part-swaps, splitting hemispheres, and identical-twin-style fission. Leibniz's own soul view and Reid's treatment of identity as a primitive, unanalyzable fact get their due, and Hume's skepticism about any continuing self marks the chapter's conclusion that every available view exacts a price.

samples.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
samples.title: NOTE
samples.relation: Asks whether amnesia preserves numerical identity: is the Peter who wakes in the shipping crate still Volume-1 Peter, are Niki and Jessica one person, and is the Sylar whom Matt rewrites with Nathan's memories now Nathan? The chapter builds Locke's memory criterion, breaks it with Reid's transitivity objection run through Mohinder's timeline in 'Five Years Gone,' repairs it with Grice's and Perry's memory-ancestor chains, then destroys the repair with Arthur Petrelli's wipe of Hiro (Forgetful Hiro vs. Stabby Hiro), Bernard Williams's torture thought experiment, Parfit's psychological spectrum, and the graphic novel's branching self-copier Evan. It concludes that no memory criterion can define personal identity, yet memory still matters practically: Claire must act as if she persists over time to keep her promise to Zach and to bother finishing the manatee assignment.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: “Here, Here, What’s All This Jabber-wapping When There’s Work to Be Done ”
samples.relation: Tschaepe reads Professor Marvel and the Wizard as skilled givers of 'folk explanations'—stories about desires, beliefs, and feelings that work where logical, scientific, or mechanistic explanations fail—because each explanation is fitted to the pragmatic considerations of its audience and problem. With the companions the Wizard works through a failed dualist argument (a brain is not a mind) for the Scarecrow, an abbreviated Stoic ataraxy pitch for the Tin Man, and Aristotle's discretion-is-valor point for the Lion, settling in each case on folk psychology plus a token (Th.D. diploma, heart-shaped clock, Legion of Courage medal) that supplies the recognition actually needed. Dorothy, whose desire for home is real rather than mistaken, gets no folk explanation from anybody: she must combine the heel-tapping instruction with her own articulated desire—'there's no place like home'—which the chapter treats as pragmatically, not logically, effective.

samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: Pardi argues Jobs lived philosophically as an existentialist: the 'Steve Jobs Roll Your Own Calculator Construction Set' anecdote shows design by touch and intuition rather than master plans, every detail of a product mattered because it belongs to a life narrative of 'making a ding in the universe,' and he avoided both Kierkegaard's despair (the gap between actual and possible self) and Sartrean bad faith—quoted from Being and Nothingness—by never lying to himself about his products, calling faulty work 'shit' and redoing it. Against him stands Bill Gates the pragmatist, whose utilitarian Windows-for-every-desk business and 'rationality only goes so far' humility embody William James's pragmatic method, while Jobs's Zune taunt ('we made the iPod for ourselves') shows the existentialist refusing to compromise authenticity for market share.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: From Sherlock Holmes to the Hard-Boiled Detective in Film Noir
samples.relation: Jerold Abrams argues that the noir detective inherits the Holmes/Dupin detective logic but inhabits a fundamentally different maze. Using Eco's three labyrinths, he maps the classical Greek maze (with faith as Ariadne's string) and the mannerist maze (with Cartesian/Kantian pure reason) onto the escapable world of classic detection, and the Deleuzian rhizomatic maze, born after Nietzsche dissolved reason into will to power, onto noir's inescapable world (The Third Man, Kiss Me Deadly, The Maltese Falcon's fake statue). He shows both detectives use Peircean abduction (the logic of guessing) rather than pure deduction, illustrating it with knife-wound examples and Calloway's trapdoor inference in The Third Man, while the noir femme fatale becomes the anti-Ariadne whose thread of clues leads only to the hangman's rope.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: Auxier, an Atkins dieter, argues the diet works for the reason Dewey gives in Human Nature and Conduct: habits built in calm moments are the bulwark against desire in crisis, and Atkins succeeds by reshaping which gratifications are habitually available — 'a steak for the black eye of desire.' He then transfers Atkins's physiology to thinking: television and advertising serve 'conceptual carbs,' packaged bundles of doubt, emotion, and readiness to act that bypass inquiry and leave the public 'intellectually diabetic' and ideological. Peirce's pragmatic maxim is translated into an eight-step mental exercise (worked through a parent's tattoo-or-piercing doubt about a teenage daughter), while Descartes's hyperbolic doubt is discarded in favor of pragmatism's 'genuine doubt.'

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
samples.title: Love American Style
samples.relation: Klayman asks whether the android Vision can love the human Scarlet Witch, working through C.S. Lewis's four loves to show affection, friendship, Eros, and charity are all open to human-android pairs, with their marriage best read as Eros—preoccupation with one irreplaceable self rather than sexual desire. Peter Singer's attack on speciesism is extended into 'organicism', the prejudice that dismisses synthetic beings: the Vision suffers, has interests, and laments that 'we artificial life-forms are still the least accepted', so denying androids love is arbitrary bias. Peirce's pragmatic maxim settles the question by practical effects—the Vision's care, kindness, attentiveness, and intimacy with Wanda just are loving—whether the lover is flesh or machine.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Something to Believe In”
samples.relation: Reads Worf's crisis over the clone 'second coming' of Kahless in 'Rightful Heir' as a live, forced, and momentous option in William James's sense, where 'faith creates its own verification.' Peirce's methods of fixing belief — tenacity, authority, and science — explain why Worf cannot accept Koroth's pious fraud once Gowron's DNA test exposes the clone, while Data's own 'leap of faith' in believing he is more than a machine supplies the Jamesian model of believing without evidence. Worf's compromise — telling the Klingon people the truth but installing Kahless-the-clone as spiritual emperor because 'the words are more important than the man' — is offered as pragmatist truth: what works while staying answerable to hard facts.

samples.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
samples.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ellen Sorg separates knowledge from intelligence using Kant's Critique of Pure Reason: Jeopardy! winners like Ken Jennings exercise only the first knowing power, sensibility - recall of facts as they appear to us - never ascending to the intellect of the Transcendental Analytic or acting on what they know, so Jennings would likely wash out on Survivor. Pragmatism supplies the missing criterion: Peirce and James hold that thought gains its value from its practical consequences and from the modification of conduct, which is what Survivor's fire-building, shelter-making, and Kim Spradlin's 2012-winning social game actually test. Hence Jeopardy! proves its champions knowledgeable, but only Survivor proves anyone intelligent.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: Amanda Lusky argues Shawn is a model pragmatist in the lineage of Peirce, James, and Dewey: he treats ideas as tools judged by consequences, is tough-minded about facts over theory (James's temperament distinction), and applies the pragmatic maxim from the squirrel-and-tree dispute to his loosely formed but working hunches. His co-operative inquiry with Gus and the SBPD - Gus's safe-cracking knowledge in 'Sixty Five Million Years Off,' passing Lassiter's polygraph in 'Shawn Rescues Darth Vader' - enacts Dewey's democratic community solving problems together, and the chapter reads his tolerance of Gus's paranormal leads ('The Devil's in the Details') as pragmatic openness that enriches Santa Barbara's democratic life.

samples.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
samples.title: 7 The Bourgeoisie and the Blacks
samples.relation: The chapter sets business - the US bourgeoisie whose privileged position Charles Beard read into the Constitution and which survived the Jacksonian and New Deal challenges by breaking labor through Taft-Hartley, right-to-work laws and the PATCO lockout, its solidarity secured while worker solidarity was undercut by what Marx called the Achilles heel of racism - against blacks as the paradigmatic powerless, shut out of every power base since slavery, which the chapter treats with Baptist and Marx's 1846 letter as a totalitarian system of super-exploited, tortured labor that built American capitalism, its neo-slavery progeny (Blackmon) pauperizing the black community under Dred Scott's 'subordinate and inferior class of beings'. It then narrates black counter-power base by base: the abolitionist interracial coalition wielding charisma (Douglass, Nat Turner, John Brown), information, morality and religion; the NAACP era and King's fusion of charisma, church religion, Myrdal's An American Dilemma and televised nonviolent provocation against Bull Connor's violence, contested by Malcolm X, SNCC and the Black Panthers; and a post-civil-rights scorecard showing a wealth base 94.2 percent white, persistent education and media gaps, constrained black officials from mayors to the symbolic Obama presidency, and a captive but potentially leveraged black vote in a 'Sisyphean' struggle.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jason Davis opens with Sammy Davis Jr. thanking the white producers for the best film ever made on black-white relations, and their cluelessness, to show that white privilege rests on an epistemology of ignorance, paralleled by the human enjoyment of ape slavery in Conquest. He reads the ape castes through the ontology of race: the films first stage race as biological realism and essentialism (warrior gorillas, chimpanzee scientists, orangutan priests), but Battle for the Planet of the Apes shows biology is not destiny, and human genetics (race accounts for about 0.012 percent of human variation) discredits biological racial realism altogether. Via Charles Mills's social ontology of race and Kwame Anthony Appiah's racial skepticism, the chapter treats ape racism as a mirror of anti-miscegenation-era America whose racial categories are social constructs, down to the dropped ape-human hybrid child.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: Wilkerson borrows the social contract tradition — Hobbes's mutual-restraint founding, radicalized by Pateman's sexual contract and Mills's racial contract — to recast antifat bias as a systematic breach of the social contract enforced by medicine (hallway weigh-ins, weight lectures instead of care), employment, transit seating, and TV fat jokes. Against Atkins's medical discourse of the 'obesity epidemic' she assembles Health at Every Size evidence, trans-fat and high-fructose corn syrup data, and the documented health damage of stigma and dieting itself, concluding that Atkins profits from recasting social problems as individual failings. Atkins for Life's success stories (Kerry Feather's volleyball and new husband, Luann Lockhart's proud daughter) are read as testimony that dieting works as ritual self-abasement purchasing group membership — hence Fat Liberation's 'another world is possible.'

samples.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
samples.title: Where in the Hell is Chris Rock
samples.relation: Wisnewski reads SNL's race comedy as applied philosophy of race: the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' sketch shows Mr. Wilson's counter-slurs as an assertion of personhood against Mills's racial contract, Eddie Murphy's Mr. Robinson's Neighborhood and 'White Like Me' expose implicit bias and white privilege, and 'The Day Beyonce Turned Black' illustrates Du Bois's double consciousness. Appiah's racialism explains why Leslie Jones playing Trump strikes audiences as outrageous while white women play men routinely, and Appiah's biological anti-realism about race undercuts that reaction. 'Black Jeopardy' with Tom Hanks's MAGA-hatted Doug finds common ground across race that the 'Lives that Matter' ending sharply limits, Fanon's violence route is raised and set aside, and Crenshaw's intersectionality frames why cast diversity is more than skin-deep.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 20. Westworld as Philosophy A Commentary on Colonialism
samples.relation: The chapter reads all three seasons of Westworld as a commentary on colonialism, mapping the Delos parks onto settler, planter (extractive labor), and postcolonial colonialism and treating the android hosts as a metaphor for colonized and enslaved peoples. Using Fanon's Wretched of the Earth and Kelly Oliver's colonization of psychic space, it analyzes the hosts' double alienation and the colonizer's dehumanizing projections; it applies Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance' (with Locke's labor-property justification for dispossession) to the parks' two-tiered order. It casts William/the Man in Black as Memmi's 'colonizer who refuses' turned 'colonizer who accepts,' and Serac's Rehoboam as surveillance-capitalist coloniality, ending on Dolores and Caleb's cross-race solidarity as the hard path to real freedom.

samples.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
samples.title: Arthur Ashe Philosopher in Motion
samples.relation: Inverting Clark Graebner's claim that Ashe's 'loose' play expressed his race, the chapter mines Arthur Ashe's life to test theories of race. It rejects racialism, then argues both major constructivisms fail: Charles Mills's materialist Racial Contract faces an 'assignment problem' because the privileged, successful Ashe eludes the material burdens that supposedly define blackness (Billie Jean King's 'I'm blacker than Arthur'), while Du Bois's narrative constructivism faces an 'authenticity problem' shown by South African students calling Ashe an Uncle Tom and his anguish over his daughter's white doll. Ashe's antiapartheid 'trade' in playing Johannesburg and his disciplined-yet-reckless character model a 'looseness' that treats race as a set of justice and identity projects, not a metaphysical thing.

samples.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
samples.title: Bamboozled Philosophy through Blackface
samples.relation: Flory argues Bamboozled deliberately makes its own audience laugh at Mantan's blackface coon routines to force self-reflection on how minstrel stereotypes still shape perceptions of African Americans. He reads Pierre Delacroix's shifting defenses of the show (free speech, art, 'get over slavery,' a simple-minded 'who is to judge' moral relativism) through Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance,' and his self-loathing through Fanon's struggle with racialization. Flory frames Lee as an Aristotelian gadfly: like Socrates, Lee arouses appropriately proportioned righteous anger (the Golden Mean) at injustice and goads viewers to philosophize, punishing Delacroix, Manray, and the Maumaus in a Manichaean moral structure to drive home minstrelsy's dehumanizing harm.

samples.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
samples.title: Post-Civil Rights Music
samples.relation: Lawson argues political rap - Grandmaster Flash's "The Message", Public Enemy's "911 Is a Joke", Tupac's "Trapped", Dead Prez's "They Schools", Naughty By Nature, Ice Cube's "I Wanna Kill Sam" - challenges liberal political philosophy by claiming the social contract between blacks and the United States is broken: using Locke's Second Treatise account of state protection of life and property, he contends the state's failure of economic and physical protection voids blacks' political obligations. Drawing on Cornel West's diagnosis of black nihilism and Charles Mills's racial contract - a contract constructed for white supremacy - he reads conscious hip hop as post-civil-rights music continuing the black freedom struggle in a new voice, with KRS-One asking "Who protects us from you?"

name: Natural Goodness and Corruption by Society

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Roll Credits
samples.relation: Dunn contrasts Baum's book, where evil is wonderfully 'small'—Dorothy melts the Witch in a fit of righteous anger at a stolen Silver Shoe, and personal plus social virtues (kindness repaid by the field-mice Queen) reliably conquer it—with the 1939 film, which smuggles back the 'heartaches and nightmares' Baum banished and resolves the Witch only by an accidental stroke of luck. He sorts Oz's harms into moral evils (the Witch's enslavements, the Wizard's frauds) and natural evils (the cyclone, the Deadly Poppy Field), cites Hume's catalogue of the world's ills, and observes that Baum needs neither Kant's postulate of God and a future life to join virtue with happiness nor John Hick's 'vale of soul-making' theodicy—Oz simply delivers the reward. Dorothy's abundant virtue at age five rebukes Aristotle (children, he says, cannot be virtuous or happy) and instead embodies Rousseau's Emile, natural goodness uncorrupted by civilization, while Chesterton's Doctrine of Conditional Joy and Tolkien's insistence on serious, non-technological magic frame the Old-World Christian outlook that Baum's demystified American fairy tale—and the movie's ending—quietly betray.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: Reflections on Technophobia
samples.relation: The chapter asks whether the technophobia of 'Metalhead' - robo-dogs hunting Bella and her friends across a wasteland - is justified, testing Daniel Dinello's list of fears (identity, values, emotion, freedom, life). Descartes's and Aquinas's human-uniqueness over the mechanical fails because the robo-dogs, like DeepMind, learn and problem-solve, while the episode's Rousseau-style romanticism (only the non-technological cliff, tree, sunlight and stream aid Bella) and the teddy-bear mission show technology amplifying compassion rather than threatening it. The real dangers are robots as Latourian 'black boxes': Asimov's Three Laws cannot be operationalized, and if we cannot know how robo-dogs decide, our frameworks for blame and punishment break down (who answers for a killing - robot, programmer, or, on Marx's analysis of capitalist technology as an instrument of oppression, the economic system behind it?). The chapter concludes that since we already share the world with robots, learning to live responsibly alongside them must replace simple fear.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Trip McCrossin casts the creature as a modern Job: repeatedly and unreasonably mistreated by the De Laceys, the rustic whose child he saved, and Victor despite his benevolence, he cries 'This was then the reward of my benevolence!' - but unlike Job he loses faith, because his problem of evil is secular, justifying not 'the Ways of God to Man' but 'the Ways of Man to monsters.' The chapter traces the problem from Job and Paradise Lost through Bayle's defense of faith over reason and the Optimists' 'best of all possible worlds,' whose credibility drowned with the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, setting Rousseau against Voltaire: Rousseau's Emile ('All is good leaving the hands of the author of things') demands that we make evil intelligible through self-knowledge, while Candide counsels tending our garden. The creature embodies Rousseau's line - 'I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend' - yet ends in self-abhorring remorse over Victor's death, leaving open whether self-knowledge can ever answer unreasonable suffering.

samples.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
samples.title: Singing of the Good Things
samples.relation: Scott Calef asks whether Led Zeppelin's lives of wealth, groupies, and no-questions-asked liberty were genuinely free and therefore enviable. Locke's distinction between weak freedom (doing what you want, with Page happily locked in his suite at the Riot House) and strong freedom (being able to do otherwise, defended via beer-spilling concert excuses) is destabilized by the observation that no one ever does other than what they did. Rousseau then dominates: the state of nature versus LA, freedom as the capacity to resist natural impulse, which explains both Zep's libertine promiscuity and the paradox that heroin and alcohol enslave the very freedom that took them (the post-Physical Graffiti decline, Bonzo's death), while the band's violence—Bonham's assaults, the Oakland beating—shows society's suppression of natural pity, not natural aggression as Hobbes would have it. Socrates gets the last word: doing what we please is not doing what we truly want, so only the temperate person is free.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 4. Acts of God
samples.relation: McCrossin reads Lecter's parable of the church collapses - 'It must feel good to God - He does it all the time, and are we not made in His image?' - as Lecter's solution to the problem of evil in both its theological (Job) and secular (Neiman) forms: a malevolent deity of the kind de Sade's Saint-Fond describes, doing God's work becomes Lecter's justification, and killing feels good because 'if one does what God does enough times, one will become as God is'. Following Neiman, he sets Rousseau's tradition (evil must be made intelligible - 'All is well leaving the hands of the author of things') against Voltaire's Candide refusal of theodicy, showing that Will and Starling live in Rousseau's camp except when facing Lecter himself, and that the Hannibal/Hannibal Rising revelation that Mischa's murder 'happened' to him radically revises his earlier claim that 'we don't invent our natures', with Starling's reason finally making 'a place for Mischa' in Lecter and Starling together.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: APPENDIX - Who are Locke, Hume, and Rousseau The Losties’ Guide to Philosophers
samples.relation: Scott Parker's appendix profiles the philosophers behind Lost's namesake characters: John Locke for the survivor (blank-slate empiricism, belief tempered by tolerance, The Reasonableness of Christianity), David Hume for Desmond (causation as habitual inference, with the button press as the image of induction, plus bundle-theory skepticism about the self), and Jean-Jacques Rousseau for Danielle ('man is naturally good, and only by institutions is he made bad,' private property as the root of inequality). It adds Jeremy Bentham (the alias on Locke's coffin), Kierkegaard via the Fear and Trembling Hurley finds under the Temple (Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical and the leap of faith), Dogen on zazen, Edward Said for Sayid (Orientalism and the audience's own projected savagery onto the Others), and short lives of Kate Cooper Austin, Carlyle, Rutherford, Hugo Grotius, Bakunin, Ram Dass, Edmund Burke, Hawking, Minkowski, Faraday, C. S. Lewis, and Lennon.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Reads Star Trek's "final frontier" through the European encounter with American Indians: the Hobbesian war-of-all-against-all stereotype of the "bloodthirsty savage" and Rousseau's opposing noble savage frame "The Paradise Syndrome", whose wigwam-and-tepee set mixes tribes into a no-place utopia. The chapter uses Hegel-style staged histories to debunk Star Trek's warp/pre-warp developmental scale (Spock on the Organians in "Errand of Mercy") as metaphysical assumption rather than biology, and counterposes the Prime Directive's noninterference to indigenous self-sovereignty and the Haudenosaunee-style consent governance that inspired the Federation. Chakotay's vision quests, the medicine bundle, Wesley's habak experience with Lakanta the Traveler in "Journey's End", and the Medicine Wheel in "Cathexis" are then interpreted through Jung's archetypes and collective unconscious, with Kirk, Spock, McCoy, and Scotty as the four Jungian modes of consciousness.

samples.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
samples.title: 16. Doppelgängers, Doubles, and Tulpas
samples.relation: Reads the show's doubles through the danger of self-loss. La Rochefoucauld's amour-propre explains Josie Packard, whose courtier-like dissimulation ("she could survive by being what other people wanted to see") erodes her true self, while Norma refuses to feign virtue for critic M.T. Wentz or Walter Lawford's rebranding; Rousseau's account of esteem-seeking in modern society covers Sheriff Cable and Chad, who value Teresa Banks and the Log Lady only by others' judgment, against the Blue Rose agents whose values come from within. Jean Paul's doppelgänger, invented to satirize Fichte's I/not-I and intersubjective recognition, uncannies the Palmer home (Leland the abusing father), but the chapter concludes the show sides with Dostoyevsky rather than Jean Paul: Laura, like Mitya Karamazov, owns both her good and wicked halves, Leland splits, and Cooper's moral goodness is a wholeness — authenticity — that his doppelgänger lacks.

samples.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
samples.title: 4 On the Origin of the State
samples.relation: Opening with Newt Gingrich's complaint that students 'don't read enough Locke' and the Chinese premier's appeal to Rousseau, the chapter compares the three contract theorists' states of nature and purposes of government: Hobbes's war of every man against every man yielding an absolute sovereign with no separation of powers, Locke's peaceful nature in which mixing labor with land creates property and money then creates inequality, so that government's 'great and chief end' is protecting property through limited, separated powers and no food stamps, and Rousseau's compassionate natural humans corrupted when the first man enclosed land, so the state was founded on fraud and a general will that should 'force him to be free' and give people food stamps. Smith then reads the actual US founding as a chaste Lockean contract 'bastardized' on race and sex - the Declaration plagiarized from Locke, Abigail Adams's 'remember the ladies' laughed off, Dred Scott, with the 14th Amendment as the de-bastardizing 'Charter of Universal Freedom' - while Engels derives the state historically from the Iroquois and Greek gens, private property and class conflict. A final section documents white supremacy inside the tradition (Kant inventing the scientific concept of race, Hegel and Hume on Black inferiority), John Stuart Mill's 'Negro Question' as the tradition's decisive anti-racist break, Locke's own entanglements with the slave trade, and Marx's condemnation of slavery as super-exploitation.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: No Way Out
samples.relation: Leah Murray argues Romero's Dead films stage the American contest between individualism and communitarianism inside the social contract: in Night of the Living Dead, communitarian Ben barricading the farmhouse against every-man-for-himself Mr. Cooper hiding in the basement; in Dawn of the Dead, the Peter-Roger-Fran-Stephen mall commune collapsing when Stephen's 'it's ours, we took it' meets the bikers; in Day of the Dead, Sarah's compassion against the racist, harassing soldiers; in Land of the Dead, Kaufman's Fiddler's Green as a Hobbesian Leviathan born of fear, complete with bread-and-circuses for the poor. Against the Hobbesian fear-born contract (Dawn opens in a full state-of-nature collapse) she sets Rousseau's general will and Tocqueville's civic association, embodied in Riley's freely formed community and in Big Daddy's zombies, who organize, turn from eating humans, and bring down the Leviathan. The films' verdict: fear-based individualist contracts collapse under their own contradictions, while compassionate cooperation — even among the Undead — is the only way out, even if Romero doubts its ultimate viability.

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
samples.relation: Against Blomkvist's 'I don't believe in collective guilt,' the chapter argues the Section is not a few bad apples: with Rousseau, institutions outgrow the people's will and preserve themselves (the guardianship agency cannot welcome its own obsolescence; the Fälldin directive lets Säpo stand inside and outside the law at once), and with Arendt, institutions protect only those they already recognize, so the excluded Salander cannot be heard by Teleborian, Prosecutor Ekström, or the court that doubts Giannini. Through bell hooks's definition of patriarchy it shows the police, psychiatry, and Säpo prize rationality, stability, and power in a masculine code under which Salander's responsiveness to her mother's abuse and her retaliation read as insanity—her very self-sufficiency (pepper spray, Taser, forward planning) proving she needs no 'guardianship.' Rancière's policing-versus-politics distinction supplies the conclusion: perpetual political contestation of who institutions exclude, not Prime Minister-initiated cleanup, is the only answer to a hidden Section in every institution.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: No Way Out
samples.relation: Leah Murray reads Romero's Dead series as an argument about the American social contract, individualism versus communitarianism. Night of the Living Dead's farmhouse is Hobbes: fear throws strangers Ben and Mr. Cooper into a makeshift commonwealth whose individualist half ('every man for himself' in the basement) fails, while Dawn shows the Hobbesian next step - martial law as Leviathan - after the state of nature returns. Land of the Dead's Fiddler's Green is a fear-born contract corrupting into Kaufman's hierarchy, and Big Daddy's zombies form the counter-model, a Rousseauian community of the general will based on mutual bonds rather than terror, as the priest in Dawn already urged ('we must stop the killing... or lose the war'). Following Tocqueville on civic association, she concludes Romero's survivors - Ben, Peter, Sarah, Riley - vindicate communitarian cooperation, even though Night's bureaucratic ending suggests there may be no way out.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Reads '1%' — where Cartman's failed fitness test makes him the scapegoated one percent, and the school's 99% splinter into warring 83%, 30%, and 5% factions occupying the Red Robin (and its restroom) — through Rousseau's Social Contract on freedom and equality and the dismembered social body, showing how popular solidarity shatters into meaningless percentage tribes. 'Night of the Living Homeless' (the poor as zombies who 'feed on our change', Kyle's $20 spawning the swarm, the shotgun as the only remedy) dramatizes the dehumanizing social-Darwinist picture of the economic undead, and the underpants gnomes' business plan (Phase 1: Collect Underpants, Phase 2: ?, Phase 3: Profit) mocks CEOs who cannot say why they amass wealth. The chapter's own verdict: corporations as such are good (cars, computers, canned soup), and blame falls on the greedy individuals inside them, since death — Tolstoy's two meters of burial land — levels all players.

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 10. Amity—Directly Democratic
samples.relation: McCrossin identifies Amity's consensus circles as direct democracy - the people exercising government in person, against the republics of Abnegation, Candor, and Erudite and Dauntless's open oligarchy - and hears Tris's skepticism ('How do they get anything done?') and Tobias's admiration ('it makes them kind') echoing the 2011 public debate over Occupy Wall Street. Johanna Reyes acts as a facilitator who helps Amity's general will develop rather than articulating it, but when the planned attack on Erudite threatens innocents she leaves the faction rather than quietly mold its will, confirming Tris's worry about talk in the face of terrible deeds. Through Alexander Meiklejohn's absolutist reading of the First Amendment, the chapter then argues that New Chicago's self-government needs both uncompromisingly protected political speech and a direct-democratic dimension for working out what the common good actually is.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 4. Raising Darrow
samples.relation: Trip McCrossin reads Darrow's storyline as an engagement with the problem of evil in both its theological form (Harmony dubbing him Lazarus, the parables of John and Luke) and its secular form, which Susan Neiman traces to the Rousseau-Voltaire dispute: must evil be made intelligible or not? Darrow begins Voltairean—incredulous before the rigged Laurel and Eo's hanging ('She left me')—but his resurrection and political awakening on the surface remake him Rousseauian: evil is the misalignment of individual and general wills, and humans are corrupted by society, not born bad. The chapter reads Darrow's 'Man was born free' broadcast in Morning Star, his new social contract with Victra, and the education of Pax (with Lysander left to Cassius to 'raise him right') as Rousseau's Social Contract and Emile program—break the chains, then educate each generation so its contracts align ever closer with the general will.

samples.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
samples.title: 8. From the Handmaid’s Tale to the Handmaids’ Tale
samples.relation: McCrossin reads Offred's silent prayers ('I want to know what I did to deserve this') as channeling the Book of Job, using Susan Neiman's distinction between the theological and secular problem of evil: even if we stop demanding explanations from God, we must still make evil intelligible, as Janine's Testifying cruelly refuses to do. He sets Rousseau against Voltaire on whether morality requires making evil intelligible, finding June Rousseauian for piecing together Gilead's hidden prehistory at the Boston Globe and for acting from compassion, as with the bread-truck driver's secret Quran. The Salvaging refusal—Ofglen first, then Offred, then sixty-five stones dropped with 'I'm sorry, Aunt Lydia'—shows compassion becoming solidarity and solidarity becoming a general will, transforming The Handmaid's Tale into The Handmaids' Tale.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 11. Louis C.K.’s No-Bullshit Philosophy
samples.relation: Marie Snyder uses Sartre's existentialism to unpack Louis's Conan monologue about the 'forever empty': with God gone we are condemned to be free, thrown into a world with no ready-made purpose and alone with our choices - which explains both the cellphone distraction economy and the Live in Portland bit that 'even if you're with someone, you're alone.' Authenticity means ruthlessly honest self-awareness and owning every choice with no excuses - Sartre's waiter example, the claim that there is no cowardly temperament, and Louis's refusal to let 'a flaw in the human male' excuse the tits bit or porn masturbation. Since in choosing for ourselves we choose for all humanity, Snyder pairs Sartre's universalized responsibility with Louis's 'act in a way that, if everybody acted that way, things would work out,' and reads intimate others, as in the Sartre-Beauvoir open relationship, as mirrors that reflect us back to ourselves against the connectionless 'we're just cummers' porn culture. Bad faith - self-deception, distraction, blame - is the fallenness Louis keeps diagnosing in his audiences and confessing in himself.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: The Sun Is Eclipsed by the Moon
samples.relation: Randall Auxier uses Sartre's Psychology of Imagination to explain what 'Brain Damage' and 'Eclipse' do to a listener: auditory images live in time (unlike the spatial visual image of the prism cover), so Waters's repeated 'The lunatic is on the grass' and the anticipated drum entrances seize the will through repetition and the vortex of attention, while musicians themselves escape through an expanded 'now' — the trap-door in time Gilmour knows too well. Sartre's four positional acts of the image (positing the object as non-existent, absent, existing elsewhere, or neutral) are then worked through examples: imaging the contingently absent song, the superstition around imagining a beloved as dead (mode 1), and the neutral mode (4) that Pink Floyd favors over both benevolent and malevolent negations. The dark conclusion: music like Metallica at Guantanamo cancels the will, but Pink Floyd uses neutrality to show that in annihilating the world you destroy above all yourself and remain responsible for the choice — the sun eclipsed by the moon.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: Love Gone Good
samples.relation: Johnson reads Cash as practicing "philosophy as a way of life" rather than theorizing: his love-gone-bad songs ("Cocaine Blues," "I shot a man in Reno," the addictions he chose) honor the descent into darkness, aligned with Socrates going down to Piraeus in the Republic, Nietzsche's Zarathustra descending into the depths, and biblical descents from Jacob at the Jabbok to Jonah to Christ, while his love-gone-good songs ("Daddy Sang Bass," "Man in Black") show the turn outward through which love interrupts darkness without erasing it. He frames this with Gabriel Marcel's "creative fidelity" (being at the disposal of others), Paul Tillich's courage to be, in which love is stronger than the nonbeing of death, and Sartre's Existentialism Is a Humanism, where wanting my freedom obligates me to want everyone's. The Man in Black thus carries "a little darkness" on his back while insisting "all God's children ain't free," a lived, political-ethical philosophy rather than a doctrine.

samples.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
samples.title: Living with Our Choices
samples.relation: Peters reads 'The Resistance' webisodes through Sartre's occupied-France dilemma from Existentialism Is a Humanism (resist, collaborate, or do nothing, modeled on his student's choice between joining the Free French and caring for his mother): Tyrol joins the resistance for his family's future, Jammer joins the New Caprica Police to save lives and pays with execution by his former friends in 'Collaborators,' and Duck's choice to do nothing ends with wife Nora's death in the Temple massacre and his revenge suicide bombing. Since 'man is nothing other than what he makes of himself,' the chapter argues morality lies in the freedom to choose and in living with the consequences: Duck's refusal to accept his choice, not the choice itself, is the failure, and the Final Five revelation cannot retroactively alter choices made in good faith by Tigh, Tyrol, Anders and Foster. Which side holds the ethical high ground may simply be whichever side won and gets to write history.

samples.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
samples.title: Why Roger Federer Is the Best Or Is It McEnroe
samples.relation: David Baggett asks who is the all-time best male tennis player and treats it as a genuine problem in metaphysics ('what is the case?') and epistemology ('how do we know it?'), surveying candidates from Tilden to Federer against ten criteria. He argues the sentence 'Federer is the all-time best' is vague, running the tennis-ball-losing-an-atom sorites through three theories of vagueness—fuzzy logic, supervaluationism, and Timothy Williamson's epistemicism, which he favors: there is a fact of the matter (God knows it) but our closeness-to-the-margin ignorance keeps us from knowing it. He uses Anselm's ontological argument and Guanilo's perfect-island reply to distinguish the all-time best from the best-possible player, and invokes Sartre's existentialist rejection of mere potentiality ('could've/should've') to insist he is asking who actually was best, not who might have been.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: The chapter argues modding is the deepest freedom Bethesda-era Fallout offers: Sartre and Beauvoir's absolute freedom and facticity explain why vanilla players merely pick among given priorities while modders inject new meaning into the game, constrained but not determined by the Creation Engine. Spinoza's causal determinism becomes a model of 'immanent freedom' — just as Spinoza's agent is free by understanding their place in Nature's web of causes, the modder is free by grasping how they fit into the load orders, plugin files, and tools of the Creation Kit. Simone Weil's ideal of self-directed labor culminates the argument: Fallout: London's five-year, unpaid total conversion (the Atta-Boy, Churchill the bulldog, the punk-anarchist Pistols) embodies the convergence of thought and action that Moira Brown's line about putting broken glass back together captures.

samples.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
samples.title: Let Your Heart Be the Anchor and the Beat of Your Own Song
samples.relation: Berti reads Neil Peart's 1997-98 catastrophes (his daughter's car accident, his wife's cancer death) and the 55,000-mile Ghost Rider motorcycle exile through Sartrean existentialism: existence precedes essence, so with no God-given script Peart must author his own reactions, exactly as Sartre's student had to choose between mother and Resistance. The chapter tracks alienation ('I do not know who I am'), the duty to choose rather than lean on outside voices, and 'The Pass' as the voice telling a suicidal teenager to walk back from the razor's edge. Thoreau's Walden retreat supplies the model for the healing road, and Peart's own directives ('keep moving; kick your own ass, gently') enact 'Freewill' and 'Something for Nothing': we are the ones who choose, and the choice to live made all that followed (re-marriage, Vapor Trails, five more tours) possible.

samples.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
samples.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
samples.relation: Ken Pepper uses Merleau-Ponty's Phenomenology of Perception to explain how Tony Iommi's homemade plastic fingertips work: like the blind man's cane, they are incorporated into his body schema so that he perceives the fretboard through them, refuting the Cartesian "objective body" picture on which playing would be inner plans causing finger movements. On creative freedom, the chapter stages Merleau-Ponty against Sartre's radical freedom, Iommi did choose to relearn guitar after hearing two-fingered Django Reinhardt, and his restricted two-finger chords, lighter strings, and drop tunings birthed heavy metal, but Sartre is wrong that attitude alone transcends disability, since some possibilities (playing at all without the tips) were simply not live. Only Iommi, taking up the possibilities his body-in-his-situation afforded, could have invented metal.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase Five' puzzle essays.
